africa-desert-sahara.name: Sahara Desert
africa-desert-sahara.countries: Algeria, Chad, Egypt, Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Sudan, Tunisia
africa-desert-sahara.notes: World's largest hot desert (~9.2 million km²). Covers ~31% of Africa. Ahaggar and Tibesti mountain plateaus rise within it. Bordered by the Mediterranean Sea to the north and the Sahel transition zone to the south.

africa-desert-nubian.name: Nubian Desert
africa-desert-nubian.notes: Eastern region of the Sahara between the Nile River and the Red Sea. Rugged sandstone plateau with wadis. Crucial gold-mining center in ancient Nubia.

africa-desert-kalahari.name: Kalahari Desert
africa-desert-kalahari.notes: Large semi-arid sandy savannah basin. Features the Okavango Delta, the world's largest inland delta where the Okavango River dissipates into desert sands without reaching the sea. Inhabited by the San people.

africa-desert-namib.name: Namib Desert
africa-desert-namib.notes: Oldest desert in the world (~55-80 million years). Coastal hyper-arid desert influenced by the cold Benguela Current, producing dense coastal fogs. Famous for the red dunes of Sossusvlei and the Skeleton Coast.

africa-mountain-atlas.name: Atlas Mountains
africa-mountain-atlas.notes: Fold mountain system in the Maghreb separating the Mediterranean and Atlantic coastlines from the Sahara Desert. Highest peak is Toubkal (4,167 m) in southwestern Morocco. Rich in rock phosphates.

africa-mountain-rift-valley.name: Great Rift Valley System
africa-mountain-rift-valley.countries: Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Malawi, Mozambique
africa-mountain-rift-valley.notes: Continuous 6,000-km geographic trench formed by the divergence of the Nubian and Somali tectonic plates. Extends from the Afar Triple Junction south to Mozambique. Hosts the East African Great Lakes and volcanic peaks like Kilimanjaro.

africa-mountain-drakensberg.name: Drakensberg Mountains
africa-mountain-drakensberg.notes: Main eastern escarpment of the southern African plateau ('Dragon Mountains'). Highest peak is Thabana Ntlenyana (3,482 m) in Lesotho. Major water tower for South Africa, feeding the Orange and Tugela rivers.

africa-mountain-katanga.name: Katanga Plateau
africa-mountain-katanga.notes: High plateau region (1,200 m) in southeastern DRC. World's premier metallogenic belt holding ~70% of global cobalt reserves along with massive copper, coltan, and uranium deposits (Shinkolobwe mine supplied the Manhattan Project).

africa-mountain-ethiopian-highlands.name: Ethiopian Highlands
africa-mountain-ethiopian-highlands.notes: Rugged volcanic plateau mass ('Roof of Africa') split diagonally by the Great Rift Valley. Contains Mount Ras Dejen (4,550 m) and Lake Tana, the origin of the Blue Nile River. Birthplace of Arabica coffee.

africa-river-nile.name: Nile River (White Nile)
africa-river-nile.notes: Longest river in the world (~6,650 km). Originates from Lake Victoria as the White Nile, traverses the Sudd wetland in South Sudan, joins the Blue Nile at Khartoum, and drains into the Mediterranean Sea via the fertile Nile Delta.

africa-river-blue-nile.name: Blue Nile
africa-river-blue-nile.notes: Originates at Lake Tana in the Ethiopian Highlands. Contributes ~80-85% of the Nile's total annual water discharge and fertile silt. Site of the contentious Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD). Confluences with White Nile at Khartoum.

africa-river-niger.name: Niger River
africa-river-niger.notes: Principal river of West Africa (~4,180 km). Originates in the Fouta Djallon highlands of Guinea, makes an unusual boomerang crescent turn north into the semi-arid Sahel (Inland Niger Delta at Timbuktu) before emptying into the Gulf of Guinea (oil-rich Niger Delta).

africa-river-benue.name: Benue River
africa-river-benue.notes: Major tributary of the Niger River. Originates in the Adamawa Plateau of northern Cameroon and confluences with the Niger at Lokoja, Nigeria, serving as an essential navigation artery for West African trade.

africa-river-congo.name: Congo River (Zaire)
africa-river-congo.countries: DR Congo, Republic of the Congo
africa-river-congo.notes: World's deepest river (>220 m) and 2nd largest river by discharge. Only major river to cross the Equator twice. Drains the vast Congo Rainforest basin. Inga Falls holds world's largest proposed hydroelectric potential (Grand Inga Dam).

africa-river-kasai.name: Kasai River
africa-river-kasai.notes: Major southern tributary of the Congo River. Forms part of the international border between Angola and DRC. Famous for alluvial diamond dredging along its river basin.

africa-river-ubangi.name: Ubangi River (Uele-Ubangi)
africa-river-ubangi.countries: CAR, DR Congo, Republic of the Congo
africa-river-ubangi.notes: Largest right-bank tributary of the Congo River. Formed by the confluence of the Uele and Mbomou rivers; forms the border between DRC and the Central African Republic. Proposed Transaqua water-transfer project to replenish Lake Chad.

africa-river-orange.name: Orange River
africa-river-orange.notes: Longest river within South Africa (~2,200 km). Rises in the Drakensberg of Lesotho (as Senqu River), flows west across the Karoo and Kalahari margin, forms the South Africa-Namibia border, and empties into the Atlantic Ocean (Alexander Bay).

africa-river-juba.name: Juba River
africa-river-juba.notes: Rises in the Ethiopian Highlands, flows south across southern Somalia, and empties into the Indian Ocean near Kismayo. Key agricultural river valley in the arid Horn of Africa.

africa-river-shebelli.name: Shebelli River
africa-river-shebelli.notes: Rises in the Ethiopian Highlands and flows southeast toward Mogadishu, turning southwest parallel to the Indian Ocean coast. Often dries up before reaching the Juba River in drought years.

africa-river-zambezi.name: Zambezi River
africa-river-zambezi.notes: 4th longest river in Africa (~2,574 km). Flows east into the Indian Ocean via Mozambique Channel. Features Victoria Falls (Mosi-oa-Tunya) on the Zambia-Zimbabwe border and the massive Kariba and Cahora Bassa hydroelectric dams.

africa-river-limpopo.name: Limpopo River
africa-river-limpopo.notes: Crosses the Tropic of Capricorn twice in an arc. Forms the South Africa-Botswana and South Africa-Zimbabwe borders before cutting across Mozambique into the Indian Ocean at Xai-Xai.

africa-lake-volta.name: Lake Volta
africa-lake-volta.notes: World's largest artificial reservoir by surface area (~8,502 km²). Created in 1965 by the construction of the Akosombo Dam on the Volta River, generating hydroelectricity for Ghana's aluminium smelters.

africa-lake-kariba.name: Lake Kariba
africa-lake-kariba.notes: World's largest man-made lake by volume (180 km³). Formed by the Kariba Dam on the Zambezi River. Major source of hydroelectricity for Zambia and Zimbabwe.

africa-lake-nasser.name: Lake Nasser
africa-lake-nasser.notes: Vast reservoir formed by impounding the Nile River with the Aswan High Dam (1958-1970). Sudanese portion is called Lake Nubia. Provides year-round flood control and electricity for Egypt.

africa-lake-victoria.name: Lake Victoria
africa-lake-victoria.notes: World's 2nd largest freshwater lake by surface area (~59,947 km²) and largest tropical lake. Source of the White Nile. Straddles Tanzania (49%), Uganda (45%), and Kenya (6%).

africa-lake-tana.name: Lake Tana
africa-lake-tana.notes: Highest lake in Ethiopia (1,788 m), situated in the Ethiopian Highlands. Source of the Blue Nile River. Contains monastic island churches dating back centuries.

africa-lake-turkana.name: Lake Turkana (Lake Rudolf)
africa-lake-turkana.notes: World's largest permanent desert lake and largest alkaline lake ('Jade Sea'). Lies in the northern Kenyan Rift Valley. Renowned site of early hominid fossil discoveries by Richard Leakey.

africa-lake-nyasa.name: Lake Nyasa (Lake Malawi)
africa-lake-nyasa.notes: 3rd largest and 2nd deepest lake in Africa. Sits in the southernmost trough of the Great Rift Valley. Contains more endemic fish species (especially colorful cichlids) than any other lake on Earth.

africa-lake-tanganyika.name: Lake Tanganyika
africa-lake-tanganyika.notes: World's longest freshwater lake (673 km) and 2nd deepest (1,470 m, after Lake Baikal). Holds ~16% of the world's available surface freshwater. Drains westward into the Congo River system via the Lukuga River.

africa-lake-kivu.name: Lake Kivu
africa-lake-kivu.notes: Lies on the border between Rwanda and DRC. Meromictic lake containing ~65 billion m³ of dissolved methane gas in deep waters, which Rwanda extracts for commercial power generation.

africa-lake-albert.name: Lake Albert
africa-lake-albert.notes: Northernmost of the Great Lakes in the Albertine Rift. Source of the Albert Nile. Recent discovery of significant crude oil reserves around the Albertine Graben (Tilenga and Kingfisher fields).

africa-island-madagascar.name: Madagascar
africa-island-madagascar.notes: 4th largest island in the world (~587,000 km²). Separated from southeast Africa by the Mozambique Channel. Biodiversity hotspot: ~90% of plant and animal species (including all lemurs) are endemic.

africa-island-mauritius.name: Mauritius
africa-island-mauritius.notes: Volcanic island nation in the southwestern Indian Ocean, part of the Mascarene Islands. Key maritime chokepoint between Africa and India. Agaléga island agreement with India for maritime surveillance.

africa-island-seychelles.name: Seychelles
africa-island-seychelles.notes: Archipelago of 115 granite and coral islands in the western Indian Ocean. Smallest sovereign state in Africa. Strategic Assumption Island naval communication pact with India.

africa-island-comoros.name: Comoros
africa-island-comoros.notes: Volcanic archipelago at the northern end of the Mozambique Channel (Grande Comore, Mohéli, Anjouan; Mayotte remains a French department). World leader in ylang-ylang perfume extract.

africa-island-reunion.name: Réunion
africa-island-reunion.notes: French overseas department in the Mascarene Islands east of Madagascar. Features Piton de la Fournaise, one of the most active shield volcanoes in the world. Key French military post in Indian Ocean.

africa-island-ascension.name: Ascension Island
africa-island-ascension.notes: Isolated volcanic island in the South Atlantic Ocean near the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. British territory hosting an Anglo-American signals intelligence station, GPS ground tracking station, and RAF airfield.

africa-island-st-helena.name: Saint Helena
africa-island-st-helena.notes: Remote volcanic island in the South Atlantic Ocean. Famous as the site of Napoleon Bonaparte's exile from 1815 until his death in 1821.

africa-island-cape-verde.name: Cabo Verde (Cape Verde)
africa-island-cape-verde.notes: Archipelago of 10 volcanic islands situated ~570 km off the western coast of Senegal. Sits along strategic transatlantic sea routes between Europe, South America, and southern Africa.

africa-island-sao-tome.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
africa-island-sao-tome.notes: Island nation in the Gulf of Guinea on the Equator, along the Cameroon volcanic line. Cocoa producer; joint offshore petroleum development zone with Nigeria.

africa-strait-bab-el-mandeb.name: Bab-el-Mandeb Strait
africa-strait-bab-el-mandeb.notes: Strategic chokepoint ('Gate of Tears') connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and Arabian Sea. Narrowest width ~29 km, bisected by Perim Island. Critical route for Persian Gulf crude oil and European container trade through the Suez Canal.

africa-strait-suez-canal.name: Suez Canal
africa-strait-suez-canal.notes: 193-km sea-level artificial waterway opened in 1869, connecting Port Said on the Mediterranean Sea to Port Tewfik on the Red Sea. Eliminates the navigation route around Africa's Cape of Good Hope, handling ~12% of global maritime commerce.

africa-strait-mozambique-channel.name: Mozambique Channel
africa-strait-mozambique-channel.notes: Arm of the Indian Ocean between Madagascar and southeastern Africa (~1,600 km long, 419 km wide at narrowest). Major international shipping corridor for giant crude supertankers bypassing the Suez Canal.

europe-mountain-cantabrian.name: Cantabrian Mountains
europe-mountain-cantabrian.mnemonic: C P A C B (C - Cantabrian)
europe-mountain-cantabrian.notes: Mountain range in northern Spain running parallel to the Bay of Biscay coast for ~300 km. Picos de Europa limestone massif. Historical coal and iron mining center.

europe-mountain-pyrenees.name: Pyrenees Mountains
europe-mountain-pyrenees.mnemonic: C P A C B (P - Pyrenees)
europe-mountain-pyrenees.notes: Natural mountain barrier separating the Iberian Peninsula from the rest of continental Europe, stretching ~430 km between the Bay of Biscay and Mediterranean Sea. Highest peak is Aneto (3,404 m). Encloses the microstate of Andorra.

europe-mountain-alps.name: The Alps
europe-mountain-alps.countries: France, Switzerland, Italy, Austria, Germany, Slovenia, Liechtenstein
europe-mountain-alps.mnemonic: C P A C B (A - Alps)
europe-mountain-alps.notes: Highest and most extensive mountain range system in Western/Central Europe (~1,200 km arc). Highest peak is Mont Blanc (4,807 m) on the French-Italian border. Major European water tower: source of the Rhine, Rhône, Po, and Danube tributaries.

europe-mountain-carpathians.name: Carpathian Mountains
europe-mountain-carpathians.countries: Poland, Slovakia, Ukraine, Romania, Czechia, Hungary
europe-mountain-carpathians.mnemonic: C P A C B (C - Carpathian)
europe-mountain-carpathians.notes: Curved 1,500-km arc of mountains across Central and Eastern Europe. 2nd longest mountain range in Europe after the Urals. Highest peak is Gerlachovský štít (2,655 m) in the High Tatras. Forms the Transylvanian basin in Romania.

europe-mountain-balkans.name: Balkan Mountains (Stara Planina)
europe-mountain-balkans.mnemonic: C P A C B (B - Balkan)
europe-mountain-balkans.notes: 557-km mountain chain running from eastern Serbia through central Bulgaria to Cape Emine on the Black Sea. Gives its name to the entire Balkan Peninsula. Features the historic Shipka Pass.

europe-mountain-apennines.name: Apennines Mountains
europe-mountain-apennines.notes: Mountain chain running ~1,200 km down the entire spine of peninsular Italy. Highest peak is Corno Grande (2,912 m) in the Gran Sasso massif. Highly seismically active (earthquakes in L'Aquila and Amatrice).

europe-mountain-dinaric-alps.name: Dinaric Alps
europe-mountain-dinaric-alps.countries: Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Albania
europe-mountain-dinaric-alps.notes: Mountain range along the eastern coast of the Adriatic Sea. Renowned for classic karst topography (limestone caves, sinkholes, disappearing rivers - name 'Karst' originated here in the Kras plateau).

europe-mountain-scandinavian.name: Scandinavian Mountains (Scandes)
europe-mountain-scandinavian.notes: Run through the Scandinavian Peninsula for ~1,700 km. Western slopes plunge steeply into the Atlantic Ocean, creating Norway's famous fjords; eastern slopes descend gently into Sweden. Galdhøpiggen is highest peak (2,469 m).

europe-mountain-pennines.name: Pennines
europe-mountain-pennines.notes: Continuous range of hills and moors separating North West England from Yorkshire and the North East ('Backbone of England'). Coal deposits powered the 18th-century Industrial Revolution.

europe-river-tagus.name: Tagus River (Tejo)
europe-river-tagus.notes: Longest river on the Iberian Peninsula (~1,007 km). Rises in the Montes Universales in Spain, flows west through Toledo, and empties into the Atlantic Ocean at Lisbon via a large estuary.

europe-river-loire.name: Loire River
europe-river-loire.notes: Longest river entirely within France (~1,006 km). Rises in the Massif Central, flows through Nevers, Orléans, Tours, and Nantes to drain into the Bay of Biscay (Atlantic Ocean). Famous for Renaissance châteaux in the Loire Valley.

europe-river-seine.name: Seine River
europe-river-seine.notes: Flows 777 km through Paris and Rouen into the English Channel at Le Havre. Core commercial waterway of the Paris Basin.

europe-river-rhine.name: Rhine River
europe-river-rhine.countries: Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Austria, Germany, France, Netherlands
europe-river-rhine.notes: Busiest inland waterway in Europe (~1,230 km). Rises in the Swiss Alps, forms the Franco-German border, traverses the industrial Ruhr Valley, and empties into the North Sea at Rotterdam (Europe's largest seaport).

europe-river-thames.name: Thames River
europe-river-thames.notes: Longest river entirely in England (346 km). Flows through Oxford and London before entering the North Sea via the Thames Estuary (protected by the Thames Barrier).

europe-river-elbe.name: Elbe River
europe-river-elbe.notes: Rises in the Krkonoše mountains of Czechia (as Labe), flows across eastern Germany through Dresden and Magdeburg, and empties into the North Sea at Cuxhaven near Hamburg port.

europe-river-vistula.name: Vistula River (Wisła)
europe-river-vistula.notes: Longest and largest river in Poland (~1,047 km). Rises in the Barania Góra in the south, flows through Kraków and Warsaw, and enters Gdańsk Bay on the Baltic Sea.

europe-river-po.name: Po River
europe-river-po.notes: Longest river in Italy (652 km). Rises in the Cottian Alps, flows eastward across northern Italy draining the fertile Po Valley (Pianura Padana, Italy's economic engine) into the Adriatic Sea near Venice.

europe-river-danube.name: Danube River
europe-river-danube.countries: Germany, Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Romania, Bulgaria, Moldova, Ukraine
europe-river-danube.notes: 2nd longest river in Europe (2,850 km). Originates in the Black Forest of Germany, passes through 4 national capitals (Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, Belgrade), and empties into the Black Sea via the Danube Delta biosphere reserve.

europe-river-dnieper.name: Dnieper River (Dnipro)
europe-river-dnieper.notes: 4th longest river in Europe (~2,201 km). Rises in the Valdai Hills of Russia, bisects Ukraine from north to south through Kyiv, and empties into the Black Sea near Kherson. Strategic frontline in Ukraine conflict.

europe-river-dniester.name: Dniester River
europe-river-dniester.notes: Rises in the Carpathian Mountains of western Ukraine, flows along the breakaway Transnistria region of Moldova, and drains into the Black Sea near Odesa.

europe-river-don.name: Don River
europe-river-don.notes: 5th longest river in Europe (~1,870 km). Flows into the Sea of Azov at Rostov-on-Don. Connected to the Volga River via the Volga-Don Canal, creating a shipping link between the Caspian Sea and the Black Sea / World Ocean.

europe-lake-ladoga.name: Lake Ladoga
europe-lake-ladoga.notes: Largest freshwater lake in Europe and 14th largest in the world (~17,700 km²). Drains into the Gulf of Finland (Baltic Sea) via the Neva River through Saint Petersburg. Famous for the 'Road of Life' during the WWII Siege of Leningrad.

europe-lake-onega.name: Lake Onega
europe-lake-onega.notes: 2nd largest lake in Europe (~9,700 km²), located in Karelia, Russia. Connected to the Baltic Sea and White Sea via the White Sea-Baltic Canal and Volga-Baltic Waterway. Kizhi Island UNESCO wooden churches.

europe-island-balearic.name: Balearic Islands
europe-island-balearic.notes: Archipelago in the western Mediterranean Sea comprising Mallorca, Menorca, Ibiza, and Formentera. Major European maritime crossroad and tourism hub.

europe-island-corsica.name: Corsica
europe-island-corsica.notes: Mountainous French island in the Mediterranean Sea north of Sardinia (separated by the Strait of Bonifacio). Birthplace of Napoleon Bonaparte (Ajaccio).

europe-island-sicily.name: Sicily
europe-island-sicily.notes: Largest island in the Mediterranean Sea (~25,711 km²), separated from mainland Italy by the narrow Strait of Messina. Features Mount Etna (3,357 m), Europe's most active stratovolcano.

europe-island-sardinia.name: Sardinia
europe-island-sardinia.notes: 2nd largest island in the Mediterranean Sea, located west of the Italian Peninsula and south of Corsica. Famous for nuraghe Bronze Age megaliths and rugged granite interior.

europe-island-crete.name: Crete
europe-island-crete.notes: Largest and most populous of the Greek islands, marking the southern border of the Aegean Sea. Center of the ancient Minoan civilization (Knossos palace).

europe-island-malta.name: Malta
europe-island-malta.notes: Archipelagic sovereign state in the central Mediterranean south of Sicily. Historic maritime fortress commanding sea lanes between Gibraltar and the Suez Canal. EU and Commonwealth member.

europe-island-gotland.name: Gotland
europe-island-gotland.notes: Largest island in the Baltic Sea and Sweden's largest island. Highly strategic location commanding Baltic maritime lanes; heavily remilitarized by Sweden upon joining NATO in 2024.

europe-island-isle-of-man.name: Isle of Man
europe-island-isle-of-man.notes: Self-governing British Crown Dependency situated in the Irish Sea between Great Britain and Ireland. Tynwald is one of the world's oldest continuous parliaments.

europe-island-shetland.name: Shetland Islands
europe-island-shetland.notes: Subarctic archipelago of Scotland lying northeast of Orkney between the Atlantic Ocean and the North Sea. Strategic hub for North Sea oil and gas infrastructure (Sullom Voe terminal).

europe-island-faroe.name: Faroe Islands
europe-island-faroe.notes: North Atlantic volcanic archipelago situated between Scotland and Iceland. Self-governing territory under the Danish Realm, known for salmon aquaculture and strategic GIUK gap position.

europe-strait-gibraltar.name: Strait of Gibraltar
europe-strait-gibraltar.notes: Narrow waterway (~13 km wide) connecting the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea and separating Europe from Africa (Pillars of Hercules). High-density global shipping choke point.

europe-strait-kerch.name: Strait of Kerch
europe-strait-kerch.notes: Connects the Black Sea to the shallow Sea of Azov, separating the Crimean Peninsula from the Russian Taman Peninsula. Spanned by the strategic Crimean Bridge (Kerch Bridge).

europe-strait-turkish-straits.name: Turkish Straits (Bosporus & Dardanelles)
europe-strait-turkish-straits.notes: Two waterways connecting the Black Sea to the Mediterranean: the Bosporus (connects Black Sea to Sea of Marmara through Istanbul) and the Dardanelles (connects Marmara to Aegean Sea). Regulated by the 1936 Montreux Convention.

na-desert-sonoran.name: Sonoran Desert
na-desert-sonoran.notes: Subtropical desert covering parts of Arizona, California, and northwestern Mexico. Only place in the world where the giant Saguaro cactus grows naturally. Highly biodiverse desert ecosystem.

na-desert-mojave.name: Mojave Desert (Mohave)
na-desert-mojave.notes: Arid rain-shadow desert characterized by Joshua trees. Contains Death Valley (Badwater Basin: lowest point in North America at -86 m, and hottest recorded air temperature on Earth at 56.7°C).

na-mountain-rockies.name: Rocky Mountains
na-mountain-rockies.notes: Major cordillera stretching >4,800 km from northern British Columbia in Canada to New Mexico in southwestern USA. Forms the Continental Divide separating Pacific-bound river drainages from Atlantic/Arctic drainages. Mount Elbert (4,401 m) is highest peak.

na-mountain-great-basin.name: Great Basin & Range
na-mountain-great-basin.notes: Vast arid region characterized by alternating parallel north-south fault-block mountain ranges and alluvium-filled valleys (Horst and Graben). Endorheic basin: all precipitation drains internally (e.g. Great Salt Lake) without reaching the ocean.

na-mountain-sierra-nevada.name: Sierra Nevada
na-mountain-sierra-nevada.notes: Granite fault-block mountain range in eastern California. Contains Mount Whitney (4,421 m, highest point in contiguous USA), Lake Tahoe (deep alpine lake), and Yosemite Valley.

na-mountain-appalachian.name: Appalachian Mountains
na-mountain-appalachian.notes: Old, eroded fold mountain system running ~2,400 km in eastern North America from Newfoundland to Alabama. Mount Mitchell (2,037 m) is highest peak. Massive historical bituminous and anthracite coal reserves.

na-lake-superior.name: Lake Superior
na-lake-superior.mnemonic: Super Man Helps Everyone Ontario (Super - Superior)
na-lake-superior.notes: World's largest freshwater lake by surface area (~82,100 km²). Holds more water than all other Great Lakes combined. Contains Isle Royale. Rich iron ore ranges (Mesabi Range) on western shores.

na-lake-michigan.name: Lake Michigan
na-lake-michigan.mnemonic: Super Man Helps Everyone Ontario (Man - Michigan)
na-lake-michigan.notes: Only Great Lake located entirely within the United States. Connects to Lake Huron through the wide Straits of Mackinac. Major ports include Chicago and Milwaukee.

na-lake-huron.name: Lake Huron
na-lake-huron.mnemonic: Super Man Helps Everyone Ontario (Helps - Huron)
na-lake-huron.notes: 2nd largest Great Lake by surface area. Features Manitoulin Island, the world's largest freshwater island in any lake. Drains into Lake Erie via the St. Clair and Detroit rivers.

na-lake-erie.name: Lake Erie
na-lake-erie.mnemonic: Super Man Helps Everyone Ontario (Everyone - Erie)
na-lake-erie.notes: Shallowest and warmest of the Great Lakes. Outflows into Lake Ontario via the Niagara River over Niagara Falls.

na-lake-ontario.name: Lake Ontario
na-lake-ontario.notes: Smallest Great Lake by surface area. Lowest in elevation (74 m). Outflows into the Atlantic Ocean via the Saint Lawrence River and Seaway, providing ocean freighter access to the Midwest.

na-lake-great-bear.name: Great Bear Lake
na-lake-great-bear.mnemonic: BSA cycle Reindeer has a peg (B - Great Bear)
na-lake-great-bear.notes: Largest lake entirely within Canada and 8th largest in the world. Straddles the Arctic Circle. Port Radium on its shore was historic source of pitchblende uranium.

na-lake-great-slave.name: Great Slave Lake
na-lake-great-slave.mnemonic: BSA cycle Reindeer has a peg (S - Great Slave)
na-lake-great-slave.notes: Deepest lake in North America (614 m). Capital Yellowknife sits on its northern shore (center of Canadian diamond mining industry). Headwaters of the Mackenzie River.

na-lake-athabasca.name: Lake Athabasca
na-lake-athabasca.mnemonic: BSA cycle Reindeer has a peg (A - Athabasca)
na-lake-athabasca.notes: Glacial lake on the edge of the Canadian Shield. The Athabasca Basin surrounding it contains the world's highest-grade mined uranium deposits (Cigar Lake, McArthur River).

na-lake-reindeer.name: Reindeer Lake
na-lake-reindeer.mnemonic: BSA cycle Reindeer has a peg (Reindeer)
na-lake-reindeer.notes: Large glacial lake with Deep Bay, an ancient meteorite impact crater (13 km wide, 220 m deep). Drains into the Churchill River system.

na-lake-winnipeg.name: Lake Winnipeg
na-lake-winnipeg.mnemonic: BSA cycle Reindeer has a peg (peg - Winnipeg)
na-lake-winnipeg.notes: 11th largest freshwater lake in the world. Remnant of prehistoric glacial Lake Agassiz. Receives the Saskatchewan, Red, and Winnipeg rivers, and drains northeast via the Nelson River into Hudson Bay.

na-river-yukon.name: Yukon River
na-river-yukon.notes: Flows 3,190 km through northwestern Canada and central Alaska to empty into the Bering Sea. Site of the famous 1896-1899 Klondike Gold Rush.

na-river-mackenzie.name: Mackenzie River
na-river-mackenzie.notes: Longest river in Canada (4,241 km with Peace/Finlay headwaters) and 2nd longest in North America. Rises from Great Slave Lake and empties into the Beaufort Sea (Arctic Ocean).

na-river-saskatchewan.name: Saskatchewan River
na-river-saskatchewan.notes: Major prairie river formed by the North and South Saskatchewan rivers, flowing east into Lake Winnipeg. Core agricultural irrigation artery in Canada's grain belt.

na-river-nelson.name: Nelson River
na-river-nelson.notes: Flows 644 km from Lake Winnipeg into Hudson Bay at Port Nelson. Major source of hydroelectricity for Manitoba Hydro.

na-river-columbia.name: Columbia River
na-river-columbia.notes: Largest river flowing into the Pacific Ocean from North America by volume. Grand Coulee Dam is the largest electric power producing facility in the United States.

na-river-snake.name: Snake River
na-river-snake.notes: Largest tributary of the Columbia River. Carves through Hells Canyon (deepest river gorge in North America, 2,436 m, deeper than the Grand Canyon).

na-river-colorado.name: Colorado River
na-river-colorado.notes: Flows 2,330 km across the arid American Southwest. Carved the Grand Canyon in northern Arizona. Controlled by Hoover Dam (Lake Mead). Heavy agricultural diversion means it rarely reaches the Gulf of California.

na-river-mississippi.name: Mississippi River
na-river-mississippi.notes: Chief river of the 2nd largest drainage basin in the world (after the Amazon). Originates at Lake Itasca in Minnesota and empties into the Gulf of Mexico south of New Orleans via a birdfoot delta.

na-river-missouri.name: Missouri River
na-river-missouri.notes: Longest river in North America (3,767 km). Rises in the Rocky Mountains of Montana and joins the Mississippi River just north of St. Louis, Missouri ('Big Muddy').

na-river-ohio.name: Ohio River
na-river-ohio.notes: Largest tributary by volume of the Mississippi River. Formed at Pittsburgh by the confluence of the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers, flowing 1,579 km to Cairo, Illinois.

na-river-rio-grande.name: Rio Grande (Río Bravo)
na-river-rio-grande.notes: Flows 3,051 km from Colorado to the Gulf of Mexico. Forms ~2,000 km of the international border between the United States (Texas) and Mexico.

na-island-bermuda.name: Bermuda
na-island-bermuda.notes: Isolated British Overseas Territory in the North Atlantic Ocean. Northernmost coral reef formation in the Atlantic. Renowned offshore financial and reinsurance hub.

na-island-baffin.name: Baffin Island
na-island-baffin.notes: Largest island in Canada and 5th largest in the world (~507,451 km²). Home to the Inuit territory capital of Iqaluit. High Arctic glaciers and fjords.

na-island-ellesmere.name: Ellesmere Island
na-island-ellesmere.notes: Northernmost island in the Canadian Arctic Archipelago and 10th largest in the world. Features Alert, the northernmost permanently inhabited settlement on Earth.

na-strait-denmark.name: Denmark Strait
na-strait-denmark.notes: Oceanic strait separating Greenland from Iceland (~480 km long, 290 km wide). Connects the Arctic Ocean / Greenland Sea to the North Atlantic. Features the world's largest known underwater waterfall (Denmark Strait cataract: cold water plunges 3,500 m).

na-strait-nares.name: Nares Strait
na-strait-nares.notes: Narrow channel separating northern Ellesmere Island from northwestern Greenland. Connects Baffin Bay to the Lincoln Sea in the Arctic Ocean. Features Hans Island (divided peacefully between Canada and Denmark in 2022 'Whisky War').

na-strait-davis.name: Davis Strait
na-strait-davis.notes: Broad strait connecting the Labrador Sea (Atlantic Ocean) with Baffin Bay. Separates mid-western Greenland from Nunavut's Baffin Island.

na-strait-panama-canal.name: Panama Canal
na-strait-panama-canal.notes: 82-km artificial waterway opened in 1914 cutting through the Isthmus of Panama, connecting the Atlantic and Pacific oceans. Expanded in 2016 with Neopanamax locks.

sa-desert-atacama.name: Atacama Desert
sa-desert-atacama.notes: Driest non-polar desert on Earth, sandwiched between the Pacific coastal range and the Andes. Cold Humboldt Current and Pacific anticyclone cause extreme aridity. Contains the Salar de Atacama (richest lithium brine reserves in the world) and astronomical observatories like ALMA.

sa-desert-patagonia.name: Patagonian Desert
sa-desert-patagonia.notes: Largest desert in South America and 8th largest in the world (~673,000 km²). Cold winter desert created by the Andes mountain rain-shadow effect blocking Pacific moisture. Sheep farming and Vaca Muerta shale deposits.

sa-mountain-andes.name: Cordillera de los Andes
sa-mountain-andes.countries: Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile, Argentina
sa-mountain-andes.notes: Longest continental mountain range in the world (~7,000 km long, 200-700 km wide). Formed by the subduction of the Nazca Plate under the South American Plate. Highest peak is Mount Aconcagua (6,961 m) in Argentina (highest outside Asia). Hosts the Altiplano high plateau.

sa-mountain-brazilian-highlands.name: Brazilian Highlands (Planalto Central)
sa-mountain-brazilian-highlands.notes: Extensive geographical region covering most of eastern, southern, and central Brazil (~4.5 million km²). Ancient eroded crystalline shield rich in iron ore (Quadrilátero Ferrífero in Minas Gerais), manganese, bauxite, and gold. Source of the Paraná and São Francisco rivers.

sa-mountain-mato-grosso.name: Mato Grosso Plateau
sa-mountain-mato-grosso.notes: Ancient sandstone plateau in west-central Brazil forming the divide between the Amazon River basin to the north and the Paraguay-Paraná river basin to the south. Global agribusiness powerhouse for soybean and cattle production.

sa-mountain-guiana-highlands.name: Guiana Highlands
sa-mountain-guiana-highlands.notes: Precambrian geological shield in northern South America. Characterized by flat-topped table mountains called 'Tepuis' (Mount Roraima). Contains Angel Falls (Salto Ángel, 979 m), the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall.

sa-lake-titicaca.name: Lake Titicaca
sa-lake-titicaca.notes: Highest commercially navigable body of water in the world (3,812 m elevation) and largest lake in South America by volume. Sits on the high Altiplano plateau. Uros indigenous people live on floating totora reed islands.

sa-lake-poopo.name: Lake Poopó
sa-lake-poopo.notes: Saline endorheic lake on the Bolivian Altiplano fed by the Desaguadero River from Lake Titicaca. Due to climate change, glacial melt reduction, and mining diversions, it almost completely dried up in 2015.

sa-lake-maracaibo.name: Lake Maracaibo
sa-lake-maracaibo.notes: Large brackish tidal bay/inlet connected to the Gulf of Venezuela. Largest lake in South America (~13,210 km²). Major petroleum-producing basin of Venezuela. World capital of lightning storms (Catatumbo lightning phenomenon: up to 280 strikes per hour).

sa-lake-patos-lagoon.name: Lagoa dos Patos (Patos Lagoon)
sa-lake-patos-lagoon.notes: Largest barrier coastal lagoon in South America (~10,100 km²), situated in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. Separated from the Atlantic Ocean by a sandy peninsula. Port of Rio Grande at its southern outlet.

sa-island-falkland.name: Falkland Islands (Islas Malvinas)
sa-island-falkland.notes: South Atlantic archipelago ~480 km east of the Patagonian coast. British Overseas Territory (disputed with Argentina, 1982 Falklands War). Key squid fisheries and offshore petroleum exploration.

sa-island-galapagos.name: Galápagos Islands
sa-island-galapagos.notes: Volcanic archipelago on the Equator in the Pacific Ocean ~1,000 km west of Ecuador. UNESCO World Heritage marine reserve. Famous for Charles Darwin's 1835 visit aboard HMS Beagle, which inspired his theory of evolution by natural selection.

sa-river-orinoco.name: Orinoco River
sa-river-orinoco.notes: One of the longest river systems in South America (~2,250 km). Originates in the Parima Mountains; Casiquiare canal connects it naturally to the Amazon basin. Empties into the Atlantic Ocean. Orinoco Belt holds world's largest extra-heavy crude oil reserves.

sa-river-essequibo.name: Essequibo River
sa-river-essequibo.notes: Largest river in Guyana and largest between the Orinoco and Amazon. Drains two-thirds of Guyana. The Essequibo territory west of the river is subject to an active territorial claim by Venezuela.

sa-river-amazon.name: Amazon River
sa-river-amazon.notes: World's largest river by discharge volume (accounts for ~20% of all global river flow entering oceans). Originates from the Ucayali-Marañón confluence in the Peruvian Andes, crosses the Amazon rainforest, and empties into the Atlantic Ocean at Belém. Has over 1,100 tributaries.

sa-river-madeira.name: Madeira River
sa-river-madeira.notes: Largest tributary of the Amazon River (~3,380 km with Mamoré). Formed by the junction of the Beni and Mamoré rivers. Jirau and Santo Antônio hydroelectric dams.

sa-river-sao-francisco.name: São Francisco River
sa-river-sao-francisco.notes: Longest river entirely within Brazil (~2,914 km, 'river of national unity'). Originates in Minas Gerais and cuts through the semi-arid Sertão of northeastern Brazil to empty into the Atlantic Ocean. Massive transbasin water diversion project.

sa-river-parana.name: Paraná River (Paraná-Paraguay System)
sa-river-parana.notes: 2nd longest river in South America (~4,880 km). Traverses Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina. Hosts the Itaipu Dam (world's 2nd largest hydroelectric dam by capacity) on Brazil-Paraguay border. Merges with Uruguay River to form the Río de la Plata estuary.

wa-desert-rub-al-khali.name: Rub' al Khali (Empty Quarter)
wa-desert-rub-al-khali.notes: World's largest continuous sand desert (~650,000 km²), covering most of the southern Arabian Peninsula. Features towering star dunes up to 250 m high. Contains the giant Shaybah oil field.

wa-desert-dasht-e-kavir.name: Dasht-e Kavir (Great Salt Desert)
wa-desert-dasht-e-kavir.notes: Large desert plateau in the middle of the Iranian Plateau southeast of the Alborz mountains (~77,600 km²). Surface dominated by treacherous salt crusts (kavirs) over muddy quagmires.

wa-desert-dasht-e-lut.name: Dasht-e Lut (Lut Desert)
wa-desert-dasht-e-lut.notes: Vast salt desert in southeastern Iran. UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for giant yardangs (kaluts) and the highest land skin surface temperatures ever recorded by NASA satellites (over 70.7°C at Gandom Beryan).

wa-mountain-zagros.name: Zagros Mountains
wa-mountain-zagros.notes: Spans ~1,600 km from northwestern Iran to the Strait of Hormuz. Fold-and-thrust belt formed by the collision of the Arabian Plate under the Eurasian Plate. Southwestern foothills contain almost all of Iran's oil reserves (Khuzestan).

wa-mountain-alborz.name: Alborz Mountains (Elburz)
wa-mountain-alborz.notes: Range in northern Iran wrapping around the southern rim of the Caspian Sea. Acts as a climatic barrier keeping moisture in the Caspian lowlands. Contains Mount Damavand (5,610 m), the highest volcano in Asia.

wa-mountain-taurus.name: Taurus Mountains
wa-mountain-taurus.notes: Mountain complex in southern Turkey running parallel to the Mediterranean coast, separating the central Anatolian Plateau from the Mediterranean coastal plain. Headwaters of the Tigris and Euphrates rise in eastern Taurus extensions.

wa-river-tigris.name: Tigris River
wa-river-tigris.notes: Eastern of the two great rivers defining Mesopotamia (~1,750 km). Rises in Lake Hazar in the Taurus Mountains of Turkey, flows past Mosul and Baghdad in Iraq, confluences with the Euphrates at Al-Qurnah to form the Shatt al-Arab.

wa-river-euphrates.name: Euphrates River
wa-river-euphrates.notes: Longest river in Western Asia (~2,800 km). Originates from the Murat and Karasu rivers in eastern Turkey (Atatürk Dam / GAP project), traverses northern Syria (Lake Assad), enters Iraq, and empties into the Persian Gulf via Shatt al-Arab.

wa-lake-dead-sea.name: Dead Sea
wa-lake-dead-sea.notes: Endorheic salt lake in the Jordan Rift Valley. Lowest land elevation on Earth (-430 m below sea level). Hyper-saline water (~34% salinity, nearly 10x saltier than the ocean), allowing humans to float effortlessly. Major potash extraction.

wa-lake-galilee.name: Sea of Galilee (Lake Tiberias)
wa-lake-galilee.notes: Lowest freshwater lake on Earth (~214 m below sea level). Fed by the upper Jordan River and Mount Hermon springs; vital source of freshwater for Israel via the National Water Carrier.

wa-lake-van.name: Lake Van
wa-lake-van.notes: Largest lake in Turkey and 2nd largest in the Middle East. Endorheic saline soda lake (high sodium carbonate content). Train ferry connects the Turkish railway system across the lake to Iran.

wa-lake-tuz.name: Lake Tuz
wa-lake-tuz.notes: Shallow endorheic hypersaline lake on the Central Anatolian Plateau. 2nd largest lake in Turkey by area. Provides over 60% of Turkey's salt consumption through evaporation basins.

wa-lake-urmia.name: Lake Urmia
wa-lake-urmia.notes: Formerly the largest lake in the Middle East and 6th largest saltwater lake on Earth. Has shrunk to ~10% of its former size due to river damming and excessive groundwater pumping for agriculture.

wa-strait-hormuz.name: Strait of Hormuz
wa-strait-hormuz.notes: World's most critical petroleum transit chokepoint (~39 km wide at narrowest). Connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. Handles ~20-21 million barrels of crude oil per day (~20% of world petroleum consumption).

ea-desert-gobi.name: Gobi Desert
ea-desert-gobi.notes: Cold winter rain-shadow desert created by the Tibetan Plateau and Himalayas blocking Indian Ocean moisture. Characterized by bare rock rather than sand dunes. Rich in dinosaur fossil deposits (Flaming Cliffs) and minerals (Oyu Tolgoi).

ea-desert-taklamakan.name: Taklamakan Desert
ea-desert-taklamakan.notes: Occupies the central Tarim Basin between the Tian Shan and Kunlun mountains ('Sea of Death'). 2nd largest shifting sand desert in the world. Ancient Silk Road routes bifurcated along its northern and southern oasis rims.

ea-mountain-urals.name: Ural Mountains
ea-mountain-urals.notes: Ancient north-south mountain range (~2,500 km) recognized as the conventional boundary between Europe and Asia. Extremely rich in mineral resources including iron ore (Magnitogorsk), copper, nickel, and precious stones.

ea-mountain-altai.name: Altai Mountains
ea-mountain-altai.notes: Complex mountain system where Central Asia and Siberia converge. Source of the Ob and Irtysh rivers. Highest peak is Belukha (4,506 m). Center of the proposed Altaic language family.

ea-mountain-himalayas.name: The Himalayas
ea-mountain-himalayas.notes: Highest mountain range on Earth, formed by the continuing continent-continent collision of the Indian Plate into the Eurasian Plate. Contains 9 of the world's 14 peaks over 8,000 m, including Mount Everest (8,848.86 m).

ea-mountain-tibetan-plateau.name: Tibetan Plateau
ea-mountain-tibetan-plateau.notes: World's highest and largest plateau (~2.5 million km², average elevation >4,500 m, 'Roof of the World'). 'Water Tower of Asia': headwaters of the Indus, Ganges-Brahmaputra (Yarlung Tsangpo), Mekong, Yangtze, Yellow, and Salween rivers.

ea-mountain-kunlun.name: Kunlun Shan
ea-mountain-kunlun.notes: One of the longest mountain chains in Asia (>3,000 km), forming the northern boundary of the Tibetan Plateau and the southern border of the Tarim Basin / Taklamakan Desert.

ea-mountain-tien-shan.name: Tian Shan (Tien Shan)
ea-mountain-tien-shan.notes: Extensive mountain system in Central Asia ('Celestial Mountains'). Highest peak is Jengish Chokusu / Pik Pobedy (7,439 m). Surrounds Lake Issyk-Kul.

ea-mountain-siberian-plateau.name: Central Siberian Plateau
ea-mountain-siberian-plateau.notes: Vast ancient upland between the Yenisey and Lena rivers (~1.5 million km²). Underlain by the Siberian Traps (massive volcanic flood basalts formed ~252 million years ago during the Permian extinction). Norilsk holds world's premier nickel, palladium, and copper mines.

ea-river-volga.name: Volga River
ea-river-volga.notes: Longest river in Europe (3,530 km). Rises in the Valdai Hills, flows across western Russia through Nizhny Novgorod, Kazan, Samara, and Volgograd, and empties into the Caspian Sea via a massive delta.

ea-river-yenisey.name: Yenisey River
ea-river-yenisey.notes: 5th longest river system in the world (with Angara/Selenga, ~5,539 km). Flows north from Mongolia across central Siberia into the Kara Sea (Arctic Ocean). Sayano-Shushenskaya hydroelectric dam.

ea-river-lena.name: Lena River
ea-river-lena.notes: Easternmost of the three great Siberian rivers (~4,294 km). Originates in the Baikal Mountains and flows north into the Laptev Sea (Arctic Ocean) via a 32,000 km² delta. Lena Pillars UNESCO site.

ea-river-ob.name: Ob River
ea-river-ob.notes: Major Siberian river formed by the confluence of the Biya and Katun rivers in the Altai Krai. Empties into the Arctic Ocean via the Gulf of Ob (world's longest estuary, 800 km).

ea-river-irtysh.name: Irtysh River
ea-river-irtysh.notes: Longest tributary river in the world (~4,248 km). Originates in Xinjiang, China, flows through eastern Kazakhstan past Oskemen and Semey, enters Russia, and joins the Ob River at Khanty-Mansiysk.

ea-river-amur.name: Amur River (Heilong Jiang)
ea-river-amur.notes: Flows 2,824 km forming the long international border between the Russian Far East and Northeast China (Manchuria). Empties into the Strait of Tartary / Sea of Okhotsk.

ea-river-yellow-river.name: Yellow River (Huang He)
ea-river-yellow-river.notes: 2nd longest river in China (5,464 km, 'Cradle of Chinese Civilization'). Rises on the Tibetan Plateau, flows through the Loess Plateau carrying massive yellow sediment, and empties into the Bohai Sea. Historically called 'China's Sorrow' due to devastating catastrophic course shifts.

ea-river-yangtze.name: Yangtze River (Chang Jiang)
ea-river-yangtze.notes: Longest river in Asia and 3rd longest in the world (6,300 km). Rises on the Tibetan Plateau, traverses southern China, and empties into the East China Sea at Shanghai. Home to the Three Gorges Dam (world's largest power station by installed capacity).

ea-river-pearl-river.name: Pearl River (Xi Jiang)
ea-river-pearl-river.notes: Extensive river system in southern China (2,400 km). Empties into the South China Sea via the Pearl River Delta (one of the world's most densely urbanized manufacturing megaregions: Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, Macao).

ea-lake-baikal.name: Lake Baikal
ea-lake-baikal.notes: World's deepest lake (1,642 m), oldest freshwater lake (~25-30 million years), and largest freshwater lake by volume. Holds ~22-23% of the world's available surface liquid freshwater. UNESCO site home to the Baikal freshwater seal (nerpa).

ea-island-kuril.name: Kuril Islands
ea-island-kuril.countries: Russia (Claimed in part by Japan as Northern Territories)
ea-island-kuril.notes: Volcanic archipelago of 56 islands extending ~1,300 km between Hokkaido, Japan, and the Kamchatka Peninsula, separating the Sea of Okhotsk from the North Pacific. Southern four islands are contested between Russia and Japan.

ea-island-sakhalin.name: Sakhalin Island
ea-island-sakhalin.notes: Large island in the North Pacific (~72,492 km²) situated between the Sea of Okhotsk and the Sea of Japan. Major center for offshore oil and natural gas production (Sakhalin-I and Sakhalin-II LNG projects).

sea-strait-malacca.name: Strait of Malacca
sea-strait-malacca.notes: World's busiest maritime transit canal / strait (~800 km long). Connects the Andaman Sea (Indian Ocean) to the South China Sea (Pacific Ocean). Handles ~40% of global sea trade, including 80% of China's crude oil imports ('Malacca Dilemma').

sea-strait-sunda.name: Sunda Strait
sea-strait-sunda.notes: Strait between Java and Sumatra connecting the Java Sea to the Indian Ocean. Location of the famous volcanic caldera island of Krakatoa (Anak Krakatau). Alternative route to Malacca for deep-draft tankers.

sea-strait-lombok.name: Lombok Strait
sea-strait-lombok.notes: Deepwater strait between Bali and Lombok connecting the Java Sea to the Indian Ocean. Marks the Wallace Line (biogeographical boundary between Asian and Australasian fauna). Used by supertankers exceeding Malacca draft limits.

sea-river-chao-phraya.name: Chao Phraya River
sea-river-chao-phraya.notes: Principal river of Thailand (372 km). Formed by the confluence of the Ping and Nan rivers, flows south through Bangkok, and empties into the Gulf of Thailand. Heart of Thailand's wet-rice agriculture.

sea-river-mekong.name: Mekong River
sea-river-mekong.countries: China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam
sea-river-mekong.notes: 12th longest river in the world (~4,900 km, 'Danube of the East'). Originates on the Tibetan Plateau (as Lancang), flows through 6 countries, feeds Cambodia's Tonlé Sap lake, and empties into the South China Sea via a vast delta in southern Vietnam.

sea-lake-tonle-sap.name: Tonlé Sap Lake
sea-lake-tonle-sap.notes: Largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Connected to the Mekong via the Tonlé Sap River, exhibiting an extraordinary seasonal flow reversal: during monsoon floods, the Mekong forces water backwards into the lake, expanding its area fivefold.

sea-island-sumatra.name: Sumatra
sea-island-sumatra.notes: 6th largest island in the world (~473,481 km²). Crossed by the Equator and the Barisan Mountain Range (Mount Kerinci). Lake Toba is world's largest volcanic caldera lake. Major palm oil, rubber, and geothermal energy producer.

sea-island-java.name: Java
sea-island-java.notes: World's most populous island (~150 million people). Economic and political core of Indonesia. Highly volcanic (Mount Merapi, Semeru, Bromo), creating hyper-fertile volcanic soils that support dense agrarian civilization.

sea-island-borneo.name: Borneo (Kalimantan)
sea-island-borneo.notes: 3rd largest island in the world (~748,168 km²). Only island in the world divided among three sovereign nations. Contains Mount Kinabalu (4,095 m). Hosts Indonesia's new planned capital, Nusantara.

sea-island-sulawesi.name: Sulawesi (Celebes)
sea-island-sulawesi.notes: Distinctive four-armed K-shaped island in central Indonesia. Major global center of nickel mining and processing for electric vehicle batteries. Sits in the Wallacea transition zone.

sea-island-bali.name: Bali
sea-island-bali.notes: Island east of Java across the Bali Strait. Renowned Hindu-majority culture in Indonesia. Active volcanoes: Mount Agung and Mount Batur. Subak traditional irrigation UNESCO site.

sea-island-luzon.name: Luzon
sea-island-luzon.notes: Largest and most populous island of the Philippines. Location of capital Manila. Contains active volcanoes Mount Pinatubo (major 1991 eruption) and Mayon (perfect stratovolcanic cone).

sea-island-mindanao.name: Mindanao
sea-island-mindanao.notes: 2nd largest island in the Philippines. Contains Mount Apo (2,954 m, highest peak in the Philippines). Rich in nickel, copper, and gold reserves. Major agricultural producer (bananas, pineapples).

sea-island-taiwan.name: Taiwan
sea-island-taiwan.notes: Separated from mainland China by the 160-km wide Taiwan Strait. Global semiconductor manufacturing powerhouse: TSMC manufactures >60% of world semiconductors and >90% of advanced sub-7nm microchips.

sea-island-spratly.name: Spratly Islands
sea-island-spratly.countries: Disputed (China, Taiwan, Vietnam, Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei)
sea-island-spratly.notes: Archipelago of >100 reefs, atolls, and islets in the South China Sea. Sits atop strategic maritime choke points and prospective oil/gas reserves. Flashpoint of Chinese artificial island building and runway construction.

sea-island-paracel.name: Paracel Islands
sea-island-paracel.countries: Disputed (Controlled by China; claimed by Vietnam & Taiwan)
sea-island-paracel.notes: Archipelago of ~130 coral islands in the northern South China Sea. Controlled by China since the 1974 Battle of the Paracel Islands with South Vietnam. Heavily militarized with radar and surface-to-air missiles.

oceania-desert-great-victoria.name: Great Victoria Desert
oceania-desert-great-victoria.notes: Largest desert in Australia (~348,750 km²). Pristine arid wilderness characterized by sand dunes, gibber plains, and salt lakes. Site of British nuclear testing at Maralinga in the 1950s.

oceania-mountain-great-dividing-range.name: Great Dividing Range
oceania-mountain-great-dividing-range.notes: Australia's most substantial mountain chain, running >3,500 km parallel to the east coast. Forms the drainage divide between east-flowing coastal streams and the inland Murray-Darling River system. Mount Kosciuszko (2,228 m) is Australia's highest mainland peak.

oceania-mountain-great-barrier-reef.name: Great Barrier Reef
oceania-mountain-great-barrier-reef.notes: World's largest coral reef system (~2,300 km long, covering ~344,400 km² in the Coral Sea). Composed of >2,900 individual reefs and 900 islands. Highly vulnerable to climate change and marine heatwave coral bleaching events.

oceania-river-murray.name: Murray River
oceania-river-murray.notes: Australia's longest river (2,508 km). Rises in the Australian Alps, forms the border between New South Wales and Victoria, and empties into the Southern Ocean at Lake Alexandrina. Backbone of the Murray-Darling agricultural basin ('Food Bowl of Australia').

oceania-river-darling.name: Darling River
oceania-river-darling.notes: 3rd longest river in Australia (1,472 km). Major tributary of the Murray River, rising in southern Queensland. Subject to severe drought drying cycles and ecological fish die-off events.

oceania-lake-eyre.name: Lake Eyre (Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre)
oceania-lake-eyre.notes: Lowest natural point in Australia (-15 m below sea level) and largest lake in Australia when full (~9,500 km²). Huge endorheic salt basin in the arid Outback that fills completely only a few times each century during rare La Niña monsoonal flooding.

oceania-island-tasmania.name: Tasmania
oceania-island-tasmania.notes: Island state of Australia located 240 km south of the mainland, separated by Bass Strait. Known for pristine temperate wilderness (Tasmanian Wilderness UNESCO site) and hydro-industrial development.

oceania-island-new-zealand.name: New Zealand (North & South Islands)
oceania-island-new-zealand.notes: Comprises North Island (active volcanism, geothermal energy) and South Island (Southern Alps, Mount Cook/Aoraki), separated by Cook Strait. Part of the submerged continent of Zealandia.

oceania-strait-bass.name: Bass Strait
oceania-strait-bass.notes: Strait separating the state of Tasmania from the mainland of Australia (Victoria). Connects the Tasman Sea / Pacific with the Great Australian Bight / Southern Ocean. Major offshore oil and gas field (Bass Strait basin).

oceania-strait-torres.name: Torres Strait
oceania-strait-torres.notes: Narrow strait (~150 km wide) between the northern tip of Cape York Peninsula (Australia) and Papua New Guinea. Connects the Arafura Sea to the Coral Sea.

oceania-strait-cook.name: Cook Strait
oceania-strait-cook.notes: Strait separating the North and South Islands of New Zealand (~22 km wide at narrowest). Connects the Tasman Sea to the South Pacific Ocean. Notorious for unpredictable strong winds and tidal rip currents.

featureList.name: Sahara Desert
featureList.countries: Algeria, Chad, Egypt, Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Sudan, Tunisia
featureList.notes: World's largest hot desert (~9.2 million km²). Covers ~31% of Africa. Ahaggar and Tibesti mountain plateaus rise within it. Bordered by the Mediterranean Sea to the north and the Sahel transition zone to the south.

featureList.name: Nubian Desert
featureList.notes: Eastern region of the Sahara between the Nile River and the Red Sea. Rugged sandstone plateau with wadis. Crucial gold-mining center in ancient Nubia.

featureList.name: Kalahari Desert
featureList.notes: Large semi-arid sandy savannah basin. Features the Okavango Delta, the world's largest inland delta where the Okavango River dissipates into desert sands without reaching the sea. Inhabited by the San people.

featureList.name: Namib Desert
featureList.notes: Oldest desert in the world (~55-80 million years). Coastal hyper-arid desert influenced by the cold Benguela Current, producing dense coastal fogs. Famous for the red dunes of Sossusvlei and the Skeleton Coast.

featureList.name: Atlas Mountains
featureList.notes: Fold mountain system in the Maghreb separating the Mediterranean and Atlantic coastlines from the Sahara Desert. Highest peak is Toubkal (4,167 m) in southwestern Morocco. Rich in rock phosphates.

featureList.name: Great Rift Valley System
featureList.countries: Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Malawi, Mozambique
featureList.notes: Continuous 6,000-km geographic trench formed by the divergence of the Nubian and Somali tectonic plates. Extends from the Afar Triple Junction south to Mozambique. Hosts the East African Great Lakes and volcanic peaks like Kilimanjaro.

featureList.name: Drakensberg Mountains
featureList.notes: Main eastern escarpment of the southern African plateau ('Dragon Mountains'). Highest peak is Thabana Ntlenyana (3,482 m) in Lesotho. Major water tower for South Africa, feeding the Orange and Tugela rivers.

featureList.name: Katanga Plateau
featureList.notes: High plateau region (1,200 m) in southeastern DRC. World's premier metallogenic belt holding ~70% of global cobalt reserves along with massive copper, coltan, and uranium deposits (Shinkolobwe mine supplied the Manhattan Project).

featureList.name: Ethiopian Highlands
featureList.notes: Rugged volcanic plateau mass ('Roof of Africa') split diagonally by the Great Rift Valley. Contains Mount Ras Dejen (4,550 m) and Lake Tana, the origin of the Blue Nile River. Birthplace of Arabica coffee.

featureList.name: Nile River (White Nile)
featureList.notes: Longest river in the world (~6,650 km). Originates from Lake Victoria as the White Nile, traverses the Sudd wetland in South Sudan, joins the Blue Nile at Khartoum, and drains into the Mediterranean Sea via the fertile Nile Delta.

featureList.name: Blue Nile
featureList.notes: Originates at Lake Tana in the Ethiopian Highlands. Contributes ~80-85% of the Nile's total annual water discharge and fertile silt. Site of the contentious Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD). Confluences with White Nile at Khartoum.

featureList.name: Niger River
featureList.notes: Principal river of West Africa (~4,180 km). Originates in the Fouta Djallon highlands of Guinea, makes an unusual boomerang crescent turn north into the semi-arid Sahel (Inland Niger Delta at Timbuktu) before emptying into the Gulf of Guinea (oil-rich Niger Delta).

featureList.name: Benue River
featureList.notes: Major tributary of the Niger River. Originates in the Adamawa Plateau of northern Cameroon and confluences with the Niger at Lokoja, Nigeria, serving as an essential navigation artery for West African trade.

featureList.name: Congo River (Zaire)
featureList.countries: DR Congo, Republic of the Congo
featureList.notes: World's deepest river (>220 m) and 2nd largest river by discharge. Only major river to cross the Equator twice. Drains the vast Congo Rainforest basin. Inga Falls holds world's largest proposed hydroelectric potential (Grand Inga Dam).

featureList.name: Kasai River
featureList.notes: Major southern tributary of the Congo River. Forms part of the international border between Angola and DRC. Famous for alluvial diamond dredging along its river basin.

featureList.name: Ubangi River (Uele-Ubangi)
featureList.countries: CAR, DR Congo, Republic of the Congo
featureList.notes: Largest right-bank tributary of the Congo River. Formed by the confluence of the Uele and Mbomou rivers; forms the border between DRC and the Central African Republic. Proposed Transaqua water-transfer project to replenish Lake Chad.

featureList.name: Orange River
featureList.notes: Longest river within South Africa (~2,200 km). Rises in the Drakensberg of Lesotho (as Senqu River), flows west across the Karoo and Kalahari margin, forms the South Africa-Namibia border, and empties into the Atlantic Ocean (Alexander Bay).

featureList.name: Juba River
featureList.notes: Rises in the Ethiopian Highlands, flows south across southern Somalia, and empties into the Indian Ocean near Kismayo. Key agricultural river valley in the arid Horn of Africa.

featureList.name: Shebelli River
featureList.notes: Rises in the Ethiopian Highlands and flows southeast toward Mogadishu, turning southwest parallel to the Indian Ocean coast. Often dries up before reaching the Juba River in drought years.

featureList.name: Zambezi River
featureList.notes: 4th longest river in Africa (~2,574 km). Flows east into the Indian Ocean via Mozambique Channel. Features Victoria Falls (Mosi-oa-Tunya) on the Zambia-Zimbabwe border and the massive Kariba and Cahora Bassa hydroelectric dams.

featureList.name: Limpopo River
featureList.notes: Crosses the Tropic of Capricorn twice in an arc. Forms the South Africa-Botswana and South Africa-Zimbabwe borders before cutting across Mozambique into the Indian Ocean at Xai-Xai.

featureList.name: Lake Volta
featureList.notes: World's largest artificial reservoir by surface area (~8,502 km²). Created in 1965 by the construction of the Akosombo Dam on the Volta River, generating hydroelectricity for Ghana's aluminium smelters.

featureList.name: Lake Kariba
featureList.notes: World's largest man-made lake by volume (180 km³). Formed by the Kariba Dam on the Zambezi River. Major source of hydroelectricity for Zambia and Zimbabwe.

featureList.name: Lake Nasser
featureList.notes: Vast reservoir formed by impounding the Nile River with the Aswan High Dam (1958-1970). Sudanese portion is called Lake Nubia. Provides year-round flood control and electricity for Egypt.

featureList.name: Lake Victoria
featureList.notes: World's 2nd largest freshwater lake by surface area (~59,947 km²) and largest tropical lake. Source of the White Nile. Straddles Tanzania (49%), Uganda (45%), and Kenya (6%).

featureList.name: Lake Tana
featureList.notes: Highest lake in Ethiopia (1,788 m), situated in the Ethiopian Highlands. Source of the Blue Nile River. Contains monastic island churches dating back centuries.

featureList.name: Lake Turkana (Lake Rudolf)
featureList.notes: World's largest permanent desert lake and largest alkaline lake ('Jade Sea'). Lies in the northern Kenyan Rift Valley. Renowned site of early hominid fossil discoveries by Richard Leakey.

featureList.name: Lake Nyasa (Lake Malawi)
featureList.notes: 3rd largest and 2nd deepest lake in Africa. Sits in the southernmost trough of the Great Rift Valley. Contains more endemic fish species (especially colorful cichlids) than any other lake on Earth.

featureList.name: Lake Tanganyika
featureList.notes: World's longest freshwater lake (673 km) and 2nd deepest (1,470 m, after Lake Baikal). Holds ~16% of the world's available surface freshwater. Drains westward into the Congo River system via the Lukuga River.

featureList.name: Lake Kivu
featureList.notes: Lies on the border between Rwanda and DRC. Meromictic lake containing ~65 billion m³ of dissolved methane gas in deep waters, which Rwanda extracts for commercial power generation.

featureList.name: Lake Albert
featureList.notes: Northernmost of the Great Lakes in the Albertine Rift. Source of the Albert Nile. Recent discovery of significant crude oil reserves around the Albertine Graben (Tilenga and Kingfisher fields).

featureList.name: Madagascar
featureList.notes: 4th largest island in the world (~587,000 km²). Separated from southeast Africa by the Mozambique Channel. Biodiversity hotspot: ~90% of plant and animal species (including all lemurs) are endemic.

featureList.name: Mauritius
featureList.notes: Volcanic island nation in the southwestern Indian Ocean, part of the Mascarene Islands. Key maritime chokepoint between Africa and India. Agaléga island agreement with India for maritime surveillance.

featureList.name: Seychelles
featureList.notes: Archipelago of 115 granite and coral islands in the western Indian Ocean. Smallest sovereign state in Africa. Strategic Assumption Island naval communication pact with India.

featureList.name: Comoros
featureList.notes: Volcanic archipelago at the northern end of the Mozambique Channel (Grande Comore, Mohéli, Anjouan; Mayotte remains a French department). World leader in ylang-ylang perfume extract.

featureList.name: Réunion
featureList.notes: French overseas department in the Mascarene Islands east of Madagascar. Features Piton de la Fournaise, one of the most active shield volcanoes in the world. Key French military post in Indian Ocean.

featureList.name: Ascension Island
featureList.notes: Isolated volcanic island in the South Atlantic Ocean near the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. British territory hosting an Anglo-American signals intelligence station, GPS ground tracking station, and RAF airfield.

featureList.name: Saint Helena
featureList.notes: Remote volcanic island in the South Atlantic Ocean. Famous as the site of Napoleon Bonaparte's exile from 1815 until his death in 1821.

featureList.name: Cabo Verde (Cape Verde)
featureList.notes: Archipelago of 10 volcanic islands situated ~570 km off the western coast of Senegal. Sits along strategic transatlantic sea routes between Europe, South America, and southern Africa.

featureList.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
featureList.notes: Island nation in the Gulf of Guinea on the Equator, along the Cameroon volcanic line. Cocoa producer; joint offshore petroleum development zone with Nigeria.

featureList.name: Bab-el-Mandeb Strait
featureList.notes: Strategic chokepoint ('Gate of Tears') connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and Arabian Sea. Narrowest width ~29 km, bisected by Perim Island. Critical route for Persian Gulf crude oil and European container trade through the Suez Canal.

featureList.name: Suez Canal
featureList.notes: 193-km sea-level artificial waterway opened in 1869, connecting Port Said on the Mediterranean Sea to Port Tewfik on the Red Sea. Eliminates the navigation route around Africa's Cape of Good Hope, handling ~12% of global maritime commerce.

featureList.name: Mozambique Channel
featureList.notes: Arm of the Indian Ocean between Madagascar and southeastern Africa (~1,600 km long, 419 km wide at narrowest). Major international shipping corridor for giant crude supertankers bypassing the Suez Canal.

featureList.name: Cantabrian Mountains
featureList.mnemonic: C P A C B (C - Cantabrian)
featureList.notes: Mountain range in northern Spain running parallel to the Bay of Biscay coast for ~300 km. Picos de Europa limestone massif. Historical coal and iron mining center.

featureList.name: Pyrenees Mountains
featureList.mnemonic: C P A C B (P - Pyrenees)
featureList.notes: Natural mountain barrier separating the Iberian Peninsula from the rest of continental Europe, stretching ~430 km between the Bay of Biscay and Mediterranean Sea. Highest peak is Aneto (3,404 m). Encloses the microstate of Andorra.

featureList.name: The Alps
featureList.countries: France, Switzerland, Italy, Austria, Germany, Slovenia, Liechtenstein
featureList.mnemonic: C P A C B (A - Alps)
featureList.notes: Highest and most extensive mountain range system in Western/Central Europe (~1,200 km arc). Highest peak is Mont Blanc (4,807 m) on the French-Italian border. Major European water tower: source of the Rhine, Rhône, Po, and Danube tributaries.

featureList.name: Carpathian Mountains
featureList.countries: Poland, Slovakia, Ukraine, Romania, Czechia, Hungary
featureList.mnemonic: C P A C B (C - Carpathian)
featureList.notes: Curved 1,500-km arc of mountains across Central and Eastern Europe. 2nd longest mountain range in Europe after the Urals. Highest peak is Gerlachovský štít (2,655 m) in the High Tatras. Forms the Transylvanian basin in Romania.

featureList.name: Balkan Mountains (Stara Planina)
featureList.mnemonic: C P A C B (B - Balkan)
featureList.notes: 557-km mountain chain running from eastern Serbia through central Bulgaria to Cape Emine on the Black Sea. Gives its name to the entire Balkan Peninsula. Features the historic Shipka Pass.

featureList.name: Apennines Mountains
featureList.notes: Mountain chain running ~1,200 km down the entire spine of peninsular Italy. Highest peak is Corno Grande (2,912 m) in the Gran Sasso massif. Highly seismically active (earthquakes in L'Aquila and Amatrice).

featureList.name: Dinaric Alps
featureList.countries: Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Albania
featureList.notes: Mountain range along the eastern coast of the Adriatic Sea. Renowned for classic karst topography (limestone caves, sinkholes, disappearing rivers - name 'Karst' originated here in the Kras plateau).

featureList.name: Scandinavian Mountains (Scandes)
featureList.notes: Run through the Scandinavian Peninsula for ~1,700 km. Western slopes plunge steeply into the Atlantic Ocean, creating Norway's famous fjords; eastern slopes descend gently into Sweden. Galdhøpiggen is highest peak (2,469 m).

featureList.name: Pennines
featureList.notes: Continuous range of hills and moors separating North West England from Yorkshire and the North East ('Backbone of England'). Coal deposits powered the 18th-century Industrial Revolution.

featureList.name: Tagus River (Tejo)
featureList.notes: Longest river on the Iberian Peninsula (~1,007 km). Rises in the Montes Universales in Spain, flows west through Toledo, and empties into the Atlantic Ocean at Lisbon via a large estuary.

featureList.name: Loire River
featureList.notes: Longest river entirely within France (~1,006 km). Rises in the Massif Central, flows through Nevers, Orléans, Tours, and Nantes to drain into the Bay of Biscay (Atlantic Ocean). Famous for Renaissance châteaux in the Loire Valley.

featureList.name: Seine River
featureList.notes: Flows 777 km through Paris and Rouen into the English Channel at Le Havre. Core commercial waterway of the Paris Basin.

featureList.name: Rhine River
featureList.countries: Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Austria, Germany, France, Netherlands
featureList.notes: Busiest inland waterway in Europe (~1,230 km). Rises in the Swiss Alps, forms the Franco-German border, traverses the industrial Ruhr Valley, and empties into the North Sea at Rotterdam (Europe's largest seaport).

featureList.name: Thames River
featureList.notes: Longest river entirely in England (346 km). Flows through Oxford and London before entering the North Sea via the Thames Estuary (protected by the Thames Barrier).

featureList.name: Elbe River
featureList.notes: Rises in the Krkonoše mountains of Czechia (as Labe), flows across eastern Germany through Dresden and Magdeburg, and empties into the North Sea at Cuxhaven near Hamburg port.

featureList.name: Vistula River (Wisła)
featureList.notes: Longest and largest river in Poland (~1,047 km). Rises in the Barania Góra in the south, flows through Kraków and Warsaw, and enters Gdańsk Bay on the Baltic Sea.

featureList.name: Po River
featureList.notes: Longest river in Italy (652 km). Rises in the Cottian Alps, flows eastward across northern Italy draining the fertile Po Valley (Pianura Padana, Italy's economic engine) into the Adriatic Sea near Venice.

featureList.name: Danube River
featureList.countries: Germany, Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Romania, Bulgaria, Moldova, Ukraine
featureList.notes: 2nd longest river in Europe (2,850 km). Originates in the Black Forest of Germany, passes through 4 national capitals (Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, Belgrade), and empties into the Black Sea via the Danube Delta biosphere reserve.

featureList.name: Dnieper River (Dnipro)
featureList.notes: 4th longest river in Europe (~2,201 km). Rises in the Valdai Hills of Russia, bisects Ukraine from north to south through Kyiv, and empties into the Black Sea near Kherson. Strategic frontline in Ukraine conflict.

featureList.name: Dniester River
featureList.notes: Rises in the Carpathian Mountains of western Ukraine, flows along the breakaway Transnistria region of Moldova, and drains into the Black Sea near Odesa.

featureList.name: Don River
featureList.notes: 5th longest river in Europe (~1,870 km). Flows into the Sea of Azov at Rostov-on-Don. Connected to the Volga River via the Volga-Don Canal, creating a shipping link between the Caspian Sea and the Black Sea / World Ocean.

featureList.name: Lake Ladoga
featureList.notes: Largest freshwater lake in Europe and 14th largest in the world (~17,700 km²). Drains into the Gulf of Finland (Baltic Sea) via the Neva River through Saint Petersburg. Famous for the 'Road of Life' during the WWII Siege of Leningrad.

featureList.name: Lake Onega
featureList.notes: 2nd largest lake in Europe (~9,700 km²), located in Karelia, Russia. Connected to the Baltic Sea and White Sea via the White Sea-Baltic Canal and Volga-Baltic Waterway. Kizhi Island UNESCO wooden churches.

featureList.name: Balearic Islands
featureList.notes: Archipelago in the western Mediterranean Sea comprising Mallorca, Menorca, Ibiza, and Formentera. Major European maritime crossroad and tourism hub.

featureList.name: Corsica
featureList.notes: Mountainous French island in the Mediterranean Sea north of Sardinia (separated by the Strait of Bonifacio). Birthplace of Napoleon Bonaparte (Ajaccio).

featureList.name: Sicily
featureList.notes: Largest island in the Mediterranean Sea (~25,711 km²), separated from mainland Italy by the narrow Strait of Messina. Features Mount Etna (3,357 m), Europe's most active stratovolcano.

featureList.name: Sardinia
featureList.notes: 2nd largest island in the Mediterranean Sea, located west of the Italian Peninsula and south of Corsica. Famous for nuraghe Bronze Age megaliths and rugged granite interior.

featureList.name: Crete
featureList.notes: Largest and most populous of the Greek islands, marking the southern border of the Aegean Sea. Center of the ancient Minoan civilization (Knossos palace).

featureList.name: Malta
featureList.notes: Archipelagic sovereign state in the central Mediterranean south of Sicily. Historic maritime fortress commanding sea lanes between Gibraltar and the Suez Canal. EU and Commonwealth member.

featureList.name: Gotland
featureList.notes: Largest island in the Baltic Sea and Sweden's largest island. Highly strategic location commanding Baltic maritime lanes; heavily remilitarized by Sweden upon joining NATO in 2024.

featureList.name: Isle of Man
featureList.notes: Self-governing British Crown Dependency situated in the Irish Sea between Great Britain and Ireland. Tynwald is one of the world's oldest continuous parliaments.

featureList.name: Shetland Islands
featureList.notes: Subarctic archipelago of Scotland lying northeast of Orkney between the Atlantic Ocean and the North Sea. Strategic hub for North Sea oil and gas infrastructure (Sullom Voe terminal).

featureList.name: Faroe Islands
featureList.notes: North Atlantic volcanic archipelago situated between Scotland and Iceland. Self-governing territory under the Danish Realm, known for salmon aquaculture and strategic GIUK gap position.

featureList.name: Strait of Gibraltar
featureList.notes: Narrow waterway (~13 km wide) connecting the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea and separating Europe from Africa (Pillars of Hercules). High-density global shipping choke point.

featureList.name: Strait of Kerch
featureList.notes: Connects the Black Sea to the shallow Sea of Azov, separating the Crimean Peninsula from the Russian Taman Peninsula. Spanned by the strategic Crimean Bridge (Kerch Bridge).

featureList.name: Turkish Straits (Bosporus & Dardanelles)
featureList.notes: Two waterways connecting the Black Sea to the Mediterranean: the Bosporus (connects Black Sea to Sea of Marmara through Istanbul) and the Dardanelles (connects Marmara to Aegean Sea). Regulated by the 1936 Montreux Convention.

featureList.name: Sonoran Desert
featureList.notes: Subtropical desert covering parts of Arizona, California, and northwestern Mexico. Only place in the world where the giant Saguaro cactus grows naturally. Highly biodiverse desert ecosystem.

featureList.name: Mojave Desert (Mohave)
featureList.notes: Arid rain-shadow desert characterized by Joshua trees. Contains Death Valley (Badwater Basin: lowest point in North America at -86 m, and hottest recorded air temperature on Earth at 56.7°C).

featureList.name: Rocky Mountains
featureList.notes: Major cordillera stretching >4,800 km from northern British Columbia in Canada to New Mexico in southwestern USA. Forms the Continental Divide separating Pacific-bound river drainages from Atlantic/Arctic drainages. Mount Elbert (4,401 m) is highest peak.

featureList.name: Great Basin & Range
featureList.notes: Vast arid region characterized by alternating parallel north-south fault-block mountain ranges and alluvium-filled valleys (Horst and Graben). Endorheic basin: all precipitation drains internally (e.g. Great Salt Lake) without reaching the ocean.

featureList.name: Sierra Nevada
featureList.notes: Granite fault-block mountain range in eastern California. Contains Mount Whitney (4,421 m, highest point in contiguous USA), Lake Tahoe (deep alpine lake), and Yosemite Valley.

featureList.name: Appalachian Mountains
featureList.notes: Old, eroded fold mountain system running ~2,400 km in eastern North America from Newfoundland to Alabama. Mount Mitchell (2,037 m) is highest peak. Massive historical bituminous and anthracite coal reserves.

featureList.name: Lake Superior
featureList.mnemonic: Super Man Helps Everyone Ontario (Super - Superior)
featureList.notes: World's largest freshwater lake by surface area (~82,100 km²). Holds more water than all other Great Lakes combined. Contains Isle Royale. Rich iron ore ranges (Mesabi Range) on western shores.

featureList.name: Lake Michigan
featureList.mnemonic: Super Man Helps Everyone Ontario (Man - Michigan)
featureList.notes: Only Great Lake located entirely within the United States. Connects to Lake Huron through the wide Straits of Mackinac. Major ports include Chicago and Milwaukee.

featureList.name: Lake Huron
featureList.mnemonic: Super Man Helps Everyone Ontario (Helps - Huron)
featureList.notes: 2nd largest Great Lake by surface area. Features Manitoulin Island, the world's largest freshwater island in any lake. Drains into Lake Erie via the St. Clair and Detroit rivers.

featureList.name: Lake Erie
featureList.mnemonic: Super Man Helps Everyone Ontario (Everyone - Erie)
featureList.notes: Shallowest and warmest of the Great Lakes. Outflows into Lake Ontario via the Niagara River over Niagara Falls.

featureList.name: Lake Ontario
featureList.notes: Smallest Great Lake by surface area. Lowest in elevation (74 m). Outflows into the Atlantic Ocean via the Saint Lawrence River and Seaway, providing ocean freighter access to the Midwest.

featureList.name: Great Bear Lake
featureList.mnemonic: BSA cycle Reindeer has a peg (B - Great Bear)
featureList.notes: Largest lake entirely within Canada and 8th largest in the world. Straddles the Arctic Circle. Port Radium on its shore was historic source of pitchblende uranium.

featureList.name: Great Slave Lake
featureList.mnemonic: BSA cycle Reindeer has a peg (S - Great Slave)
featureList.notes: Deepest lake in North America (614 m). Capital Yellowknife sits on its northern shore (center of Canadian diamond mining industry). Headwaters of the Mackenzie River.

featureList.name: Lake Athabasca
featureList.mnemonic: BSA cycle Reindeer has a peg (A - Athabasca)
featureList.notes: Glacial lake on the edge of the Canadian Shield. The Athabasca Basin surrounding it contains the world's highest-grade mined uranium deposits (Cigar Lake, McArthur River).

featureList.name: Reindeer Lake
featureList.mnemonic: BSA cycle Reindeer has a peg (Reindeer)
featureList.notes: Large glacial lake with Deep Bay, an ancient meteorite impact crater (13 km wide, 220 m deep). Drains into the Churchill River system.

featureList.name: Lake Winnipeg
featureList.mnemonic: BSA cycle Reindeer has a peg (peg - Winnipeg)
