featureList.notes: 11th largest freshwater lake in the world. Remnant of prehistoric glacial Lake Agassiz. Receives the Saskatchewan, Red, and Winnipeg rivers, and drains northeast via the Nelson River into Hudson Bay.

featureList.name: Yukon River
featureList.notes: Flows 3,190 km through northwestern Canada and central Alaska to empty into the Bering Sea. Site of the famous 1896-1899 Klondike Gold Rush.

featureList.name: Mackenzie River
featureList.notes: Longest river in Canada (4,241 km with Peace/Finlay headwaters) and 2nd longest in North America. Rises from Great Slave Lake and empties into the Beaufort Sea (Arctic Ocean).

featureList.name: Saskatchewan River
featureList.notes: Major prairie river formed by the North and South Saskatchewan rivers, flowing east into Lake Winnipeg. Core agricultural irrigation artery in Canada's grain belt.

featureList.name: Nelson River
featureList.notes: Flows 644 km from Lake Winnipeg into Hudson Bay at Port Nelson. Major source of hydroelectricity for Manitoba Hydro.

featureList.name: Columbia River
featureList.notes: Largest river flowing into the Pacific Ocean from North America by volume. Grand Coulee Dam is the largest electric power producing facility in the United States.

featureList.name: Snake River
featureList.notes: Largest tributary of the Columbia River. Carves through Hells Canyon (deepest river gorge in North America, 2,436 m, deeper than the Grand Canyon).

featureList.name: Colorado River
featureList.notes: Flows 2,330 km across the arid American Southwest. Carved the Grand Canyon in northern Arizona. Controlled by Hoover Dam (Lake Mead). Heavy agricultural diversion means it rarely reaches the Gulf of California.

featureList.name: Mississippi River
featureList.notes: Chief river of the 2nd largest drainage basin in the world (after the Amazon). Originates at Lake Itasca in Minnesota and empties into the Gulf of Mexico south of New Orleans via a birdfoot delta.

featureList.name: Missouri River
featureList.notes: Longest river in North America (3,767 km). Rises in the Rocky Mountains of Montana and joins the Mississippi River just north of St. Louis, Missouri ('Big Muddy').

featureList.name: Ohio River
featureList.notes: Largest tributary by volume of the Mississippi River. Formed at Pittsburgh by the confluence of the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers, flowing 1,579 km to Cairo, Illinois.

featureList.name: Rio Grande (Río Bravo)
featureList.notes: Flows 3,051 km from Colorado to the Gulf of Mexico. Forms ~2,000 km of the international border between the United States (Texas) and Mexico.

featureList.name: Bermuda
featureList.notes: Isolated British Overseas Territory in the North Atlantic Ocean. Northernmost coral reef formation in the Atlantic. Renowned offshore financial and reinsurance hub.

featureList.name: Baffin Island
featureList.notes: Largest island in Canada and 5th largest in the world (~507,451 km²). Home to the Inuit territory capital of Iqaluit. High Arctic glaciers and fjords.

featureList.name: Ellesmere Island
featureList.notes: Northernmost island in the Canadian Arctic Archipelago and 10th largest in the world. Features Alert, the northernmost permanently inhabited settlement on Earth.

featureList.name: Denmark Strait
featureList.notes: Oceanic strait separating Greenland from Iceland (~480 km long, 290 km wide). Connects the Arctic Ocean / Greenland Sea to the North Atlantic. Features the world's largest known underwater waterfall (Denmark Strait cataract: cold water plunges 3,500 m).

featureList.name: Nares Strait
featureList.notes: Narrow channel separating northern Ellesmere Island from northwestern Greenland. Connects Baffin Bay to the Lincoln Sea in the Arctic Ocean. Features Hans Island (divided peacefully between Canada and Denmark in 2022 'Whisky War').

featureList.name: Davis Strait
featureList.notes: Broad strait connecting the Labrador Sea (Atlantic Ocean) with Baffin Bay. Separates mid-western Greenland from Nunavut's Baffin Island.

featureList.name: Panama Canal
featureList.notes: 82-km artificial waterway opened in 1914 cutting through the Isthmus of Panama, connecting the Atlantic and Pacific oceans. Expanded in 2016 with Neopanamax locks.

featureList.name: Atacama Desert
featureList.notes: Driest non-polar desert on Earth, sandwiched between the Pacific coastal range and the Andes. Cold Humboldt Current and Pacific anticyclone cause extreme aridity. Contains the Salar de Atacama (richest lithium brine reserves in the world) and astronomical observatories like ALMA.

featureList.name: Patagonian Desert
featureList.notes: Largest desert in South America and 8th largest in the world (~673,000 km²). Cold winter desert created by the Andes mountain rain-shadow effect blocking Pacific moisture. Sheep farming and Vaca Muerta shale deposits.

featureList.name: Cordillera de los Andes
featureList.countries: Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile, Argentina
featureList.notes: Longest continental mountain range in the world (~7,000 km long, 200-700 km wide). Formed by the subduction of the Nazca Plate under the South American Plate. Highest peak is Mount Aconcagua (6,961 m) in Argentina (highest outside Asia). Hosts the Altiplano high plateau.

featureList.name: Brazilian Highlands (Planalto Central)
featureList.notes: Extensive geographical region covering most of eastern, southern, and central Brazil (~4.5 million km²). Ancient eroded crystalline shield rich in iron ore (Quadrilátero Ferrífero in Minas Gerais), manganese, bauxite, and gold. Source of the Paraná and São Francisco rivers.

featureList.name: Mato Grosso Plateau
featureList.notes: Ancient sandstone plateau in west-central Brazil forming the divide between the Amazon River basin to the north and the Paraguay-Paraná river basin to the south. Global agribusiness powerhouse for soybean and cattle production.

featureList.name: Guiana Highlands
featureList.notes: Precambrian geological shield in northern South America. Characterized by flat-topped table mountains called 'Tepuis' (Mount Roraima). Contains Angel Falls (Salto Ángel, 979 m), the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall.

featureList.name: Lake Titicaca
featureList.notes: Highest commercially navigable body of water in the world (3,812 m elevation) and largest lake in South America by volume. Sits on the high Altiplano plateau. Uros indigenous people live on floating totora reed islands.

featureList.name: Lake Poopó
featureList.notes: Saline endorheic lake on the Bolivian Altiplano fed by the Desaguadero River from Lake Titicaca. Due to climate change, glacial melt reduction, and mining diversions, it almost completely dried up in 2015.

featureList.name: Lake Maracaibo
featureList.notes: Large brackish tidal bay/inlet connected to the Gulf of Venezuela. Largest lake in South America (~13,210 km²). Major petroleum-producing basin of Venezuela. World capital of lightning storms (Catatumbo lightning phenomenon: up to 280 strikes per hour).

featureList.name: Lagoa dos Patos (Patos Lagoon)
featureList.notes: Largest barrier coastal lagoon in South America (~10,100 km²), situated in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. Separated from the Atlantic Ocean by a sandy peninsula. Port of Rio Grande at its southern outlet.

featureList.name: Falkland Islands (Islas Malvinas)
featureList.notes: South Atlantic archipelago ~480 km east of the Patagonian coast. British Overseas Territory (disputed with Argentina, 1982 Falklands War). Key squid fisheries and offshore petroleum exploration.

featureList.name: Galápagos Islands
featureList.notes: Volcanic archipelago on the Equator in the Pacific Ocean ~1,000 km west of Ecuador. UNESCO World Heritage marine reserve. Famous for Charles Darwin's 1835 visit aboard HMS Beagle, which inspired his theory of evolution by natural selection.

featureList.name: Orinoco River
featureList.notes: One of the longest river systems in South America (~2,250 km). Originates in the Parima Mountains; Casiquiare canal connects it naturally to the Amazon basin. Empties into the Atlantic Ocean. Orinoco Belt holds world's largest extra-heavy crude oil reserves.

featureList.name: Essequibo River
featureList.notes: Largest river in Guyana and largest between the Orinoco and Amazon. Drains two-thirds of Guyana. The Essequibo territory west of the river is subject to an active territorial claim by Venezuela.

featureList.name: Amazon River
featureList.notes: World's largest river by discharge volume (accounts for ~20% of all global river flow entering oceans). Originates from the Ucayali-Marañón confluence in the Peruvian Andes, crosses the Amazon rainforest, and empties into the Atlantic Ocean at Belém. Has over 1,100 tributaries.

featureList.name: Madeira River
featureList.notes: Largest tributary of the Amazon River (~3,380 km with Mamoré). Formed by the junction of the Beni and Mamoré rivers. Jirau and Santo Antônio hydroelectric dams.

featureList.name: São Francisco River
featureList.notes: Longest river entirely within Brazil (~2,914 km, 'river of national unity'). Originates in Minas Gerais and cuts through the semi-arid Sertão of northeastern Brazil to empty into the Atlantic Ocean. Massive transbasin water diversion project.

featureList.name: Paraná River (Paraná-Paraguay System)
featureList.notes: 2nd longest river in South America (~4,880 km). Traverses Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina. Hosts the Itaipu Dam (world's 2nd largest hydroelectric dam by capacity) on Brazil-Paraguay border. Merges with Uruguay River to form the Río de la Plata estuary.

featureList.name: Rub' al Khali (Empty Quarter)
featureList.notes: World's largest continuous sand desert (~650,000 km²), covering most of the southern Arabian Peninsula. Features towering star dunes up to 250 m high. Contains the giant Shaybah oil field.

featureList.name: Dasht-e Kavir (Great Salt Desert)
featureList.notes: Large desert plateau in the middle of the Iranian Plateau southeast of the Alborz mountains (~77,600 km²). Surface dominated by treacherous salt crusts (kavirs) over muddy quagmires.

featureList.name: Dasht-e Lut (Lut Desert)
featureList.notes: Vast salt desert in southeastern Iran. UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for giant yardangs (kaluts) and the highest land skin surface temperatures ever recorded by NASA satellites (over 70.7°C at Gandom Beryan).

featureList.name: Zagros Mountains
featureList.notes: Spans ~1,600 km from northwestern Iran to the Strait of Hormuz. Fold-and-thrust belt formed by the collision of the Arabian Plate under the Eurasian Plate. Southwestern foothills contain almost all of Iran's oil reserves (Khuzestan).

featureList.name: Alborz Mountains (Elburz)
featureList.notes: Range in northern Iran wrapping around the southern rim of the Caspian Sea. Acts as a climatic barrier keeping moisture in the Caspian lowlands. Contains Mount Damavand (5,610 m), the highest volcano in Asia.

featureList.name: Taurus Mountains
featureList.notes: Mountain complex in southern Turkey running parallel to the Mediterranean coast, separating the central Anatolian Plateau from the Mediterranean coastal plain. Headwaters of the Tigris and Euphrates rise in eastern Taurus extensions.

featureList.name: Tigris River
featureList.notes: Eastern of the two great rivers defining Mesopotamia (~1,750 km). Rises in Lake Hazar in the Taurus Mountains of Turkey, flows past Mosul and Baghdad in Iraq, confluences with the Euphrates at Al-Qurnah to form the Shatt al-Arab.

featureList.name: Euphrates River
featureList.notes: Longest river in Western Asia (~2,800 km). Originates from the Murat and Karasu rivers in eastern Turkey (Atatürk Dam / GAP project), traverses northern Syria (Lake Assad), enters Iraq, and empties into the Persian Gulf via Shatt al-Arab.

featureList.name: Dead Sea
featureList.notes: Endorheic salt lake in the Jordan Rift Valley. Lowest land elevation on Earth (-430 m below sea level). Hyper-saline water (~34% salinity, nearly 10x saltier than the ocean), allowing humans to float effortlessly. Major potash extraction.

featureList.name: Sea of Galilee (Lake Tiberias)
featureList.notes: Lowest freshwater lake on Earth (~214 m below sea level). Fed by the upper Jordan River and Mount Hermon springs; vital source of freshwater for Israel via the National Water Carrier.

featureList.name: Lake Van
featureList.notes: Largest lake in Turkey and 2nd largest in the Middle East. Endorheic saline soda lake (high sodium carbonate content). Train ferry connects the Turkish railway system across the lake to Iran.

featureList.name: Lake Tuz
featureList.notes: Shallow endorheic hypersaline lake on the Central Anatolian Plateau. 2nd largest lake in Turkey by area. Provides over 60% of Turkey's salt consumption through evaporation basins.

featureList.name: Lake Urmia
featureList.notes: Formerly the largest lake in the Middle East and 6th largest saltwater lake on Earth. Has shrunk to ~10% of its former size due to river damming and excessive groundwater pumping for agriculture.

featureList.name: Strait of Hormuz
featureList.notes: World's most critical petroleum transit chokepoint (~39 km wide at narrowest). Connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. Handles ~20-21 million barrels of crude oil per day (~20% of world petroleum consumption).

featureList.name: Gobi Desert
featureList.notes: Cold winter rain-shadow desert created by the Tibetan Plateau and Himalayas blocking Indian Ocean moisture. Characterized by bare rock rather than sand dunes. Rich in dinosaur fossil deposits (Flaming Cliffs) and minerals (Oyu Tolgoi).

featureList.name: Taklamakan Desert
featureList.notes: Occupies the central Tarim Basin between the Tian Shan and Kunlun mountains ('Sea of Death'). 2nd largest shifting sand desert in the world. Ancient Silk Road routes bifurcated along its northern and southern oasis rims.

featureList.name: Ural Mountains
featureList.notes: Ancient north-south mountain range (~2,500 km) recognized as the conventional boundary between Europe and Asia. Extremely rich in mineral resources including iron ore (Magnitogorsk), copper, nickel, and precious stones.

featureList.name: Altai Mountains
featureList.notes: Complex mountain system where Central Asia and Siberia converge. Source of the Ob and Irtysh rivers. Highest peak is Belukha (4,506 m). Center of the proposed Altaic language family.

featureList.name: The Himalayas
featureList.notes: Highest mountain range on Earth, formed by the continuing continent-continent collision of the Indian Plate into the Eurasian Plate. Contains 9 of the world's 14 peaks over 8,000 m, including Mount Everest (8,848.86 m).

featureList.name: Tibetan Plateau
featureList.notes: World's highest and largest plateau (~2.5 million km², average elevation >4,500 m, 'Roof of the World'). 'Water Tower of Asia': headwaters of the Indus, Ganges-Brahmaputra (Yarlung Tsangpo), Mekong, Yangtze, Yellow, and Salween rivers.

featureList.name: Kunlun Shan
featureList.notes: One of the longest mountain chains in Asia (>3,000 km), forming the northern boundary of the Tibetan Plateau and the southern border of the Tarim Basin / Taklamakan Desert.

featureList.name: Tian Shan (Tien Shan)
featureList.notes: Extensive mountain system in Central Asia ('Celestial Mountains'). Highest peak is Jengish Chokusu / Pik Pobedy (7,439 m). Surrounds Lake Issyk-Kul.

featureList.name: Central Siberian Plateau
featureList.notes: Vast ancient upland between the Yenisey and Lena rivers (~1.5 million km²). Underlain by the Siberian Traps (massive volcanic flood basalts formed ~252 million years ago during the Permian extinction). Norilsk holds world's premier nickel, palladium, and copper mines.

featureList.name: Volga River
featureList.notes: Longest river in Europe (3,530 km). Rises in the Valdai Hills, flows across western Russia through Nizhny Novgorod, Kazan, Samara, and Volgograd, and empties into the Caspian Sea via a massive delta.

featureList.name: Yenisey River
featureList.notes: 5th longest river system in the world (with Angara/Selenga, ~5,539 km). Flows north from Mongolia across central Siberia into the Kara Sea (Arctic Ocean). Sayano-Shushenskaya hydroelectric dam.

featureList.name: Lena River
featureList.notes: Easternmost of the three great Siberian rivers (~4,294 km). Originates in the Baikal Mountains and flows north into the Laptev Sea (Arctic Ocean) via a 32,000 km² delta. Lena Pillars UNESCO site.

featureList.name: Ob River
featureList.notes: Major Siberian river formed by the confluence of the Biya and Katun rivers in the Altai Krai. Empties into the Arctic Ocean via the Gulf of Ob (world's longest estuary, 800 km).

featureList.name: Irtysh River
featureList.notes: Longest tributary river in the world (~4,248 km). Originates in Xinjiang, China, flows through eastern Kazakhstan past Oskemen and Semey, enters Russia, and joins the Ob River at Khanty-Mansiysk.

featureList.name: Amur River (Heilong Jiang)
featureList.notes: Flows 2,824 km forming the long international border between the Russian Far East and Northeast China (Manchuria). Empties into the Strait of Tartary / Sea of Okhotsk.

featureList.name: Yellow River (Huang He)
featureList.notes: 2nd longest river in China (5,464 km, 'Cradle of Chinese Civilization'). Rises on the Tibetan Plateau, flows through the Loess Plateau carrying massive yellow sediment, and empties into the Bohai Sea. Historically called 'China's Sorrow' due to devastating catastrophic course shifts.

featureList.name: Yangtze River (Chang Jiang)
featureList.notes: Longest river in Asia and 3rd longest in the world (6,300 km). Rises on the Tibetan Plateau, traverses southern China, and empties into the East China Sea at Shanghai. Home to the Three Gorges Dam (world's largest power station by installed capacity).

featureList.name: Pearl River (Xi Jiang)
featureList.notes: Extensive river system in southern China (2,400 km). Empties into the South China Sea via the Pearl River Delta (one of the world's most densely urbanized manufacturing megaregions: Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, Macao).

featureList.name: Lake Baikal
featureList.notes: World's deepest lake (1,642 m), oldest freshwater lake (~25-30 million years), and largest freshwater lake by volume. Holds ~22-23% of the world's available surface liquid freshwater. UNESCO site home to the Baikal freshwater seal (nerpa).

featureList.name: Kuril Islands
featureList.countries: Russia (Claimed in part by Japan as Northern Territories)
featureList.notes: Volcanic archipelago of 56 islands extending ~1,300 km between Hokkaido, Japan, and the Kamchatka Peninsula, separating the Sea of Okhotsk from the North Pacific. Southern four islands are contested between Russia and Japan.

featureList.name: Sakhalin Island
featureList.notes: Large island in the North Pacific (~72,492 km²) situated between the Sea of Okhotsk and the Sea of Japan. Major center for offshore oil and natural gas production (Sakhalin-I and Sakhalin-II LNG projects).

featureList.name: Strait of Malacca
featureList.notes: World's busiest maritime transit canal / strait (~800 km long). Connects the Andaman Sea (Indian Ocean) to the South China Sea (Pacific Ocean). Handles ~40% of global sea trade, including 80% of China's crude oil imports ('Malacca Dilemma').

featureList.name: Sunda Strait
featureList.notes: Strait between Java and Sumatra connecting the Java Sea to the Indian Ocean. Location of the famous volcanic caldera island of Krakatoa (Anak Krakatau). Alternative route to Malacca for deep-draft tankers.

featureList.name: Lombok Strait
featureList.notes: Deepwater strait between Bali and Lombok connecting the Java Sea to the Indian Ocean. Marks the Wallace Line (biogeographical boundary between Asian and Australasian fauna). Used by supertankers exceeding Malacca draft limits.

featureList.name: Chao Phraya River
featureList.notes: Principal river of Thailand (372 km). Formed by the confluence of the Ping and Nan rivers, flows south through Bangkok, and empties into the Gulf of Thailand. Heart of Thailand's wet-rice agriculture.

featureList.name: Mekong River
featureList.countries: China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam
featureList.notes: 12th longest river in the world (~4,900 km, 'Danube of the East'). Originates on the Tibetan Plateau (as Lancang), flows through 6 countries, feeds Cambodia's Tonlé Sap lake, and empties into the South China Sea via a vast delta in southern Vietnam.

featureList.name: Tonlé Sap Lake
featureList.notes: Largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Connected to the Mekong via the Tonlé Sap River, exhibiting an extraordinary seasonal flow reversal: during monsoon floods, the Mekong forces water backwards into the lake, expanding its area fivefold.

featureList.name: Sumatra
featureList.notes: 6th largest island in the world (~473,481 km²). Crossed by the Equator and the Barisan Mountain Range (Mount Kerinci). Lake Toba is world's largest volcanic caldera lake. Major palm oil, rubber, and geothermal energy producer.

featureList.name: Java
featureList.notes: World's most populous island (~150 million people). Economic and political core of Indonesia. Highly volcanic (Mount Merapi, Semeru, Bromo), creating hyper-fertile volcanic soils that support dense agrarian civilization.

featureList.name: Borneo (Kalimantan)
featureList.notes: 3rd largest island in the world (~748,168 km²). Only island in the world divided among three sovereign nations. Contains Mount Kinabalu (4,095 m). Hosts Indonesia's new planned capital, Nusantara.

featureList.name: Sulawesi (Celebes)
featureList.notes: Distinctive four-armed K-shaped island in central Indonesia. Major global center of nickel mining and processing for electric vehicle batteries. Sits in the Wallacea transition zone.

featureList.name: Bali
featureList.notes: Island east of Java across the Bali Strait. Renowned Hindu-majority culture in Indonesia. Active volcanoes: Mount Agung and Mount Batur. Subak traditional irrigation UNESCO site.

featureList.name: Luzon
featureList.notes: Largest and most populous island of the Philippines. Location of capital Manila. Contains active volcanoes Mount Pinatubo (major 1991 eruption) and Mayon (perfect stratovolcanic cone).

featureList.name: Mindanao
featureList.notes: 2nd largest island in the Philippines. Contains Mount Apo (2,954 m, highest peak in the Philippines). Rich in nickel, copper, and gold reserves. Major agricultural producer (bananas, pineapples).

featureList.name: Taiwan
featureList.notes: Separated from mainland China by the 160-km wide Taiwan Strait. Global semiconductor manufacturing powerhouse: TSMC manufactures >60% of world semiconductors and >90% of advanced sub-7nm microchips.

featureList.name: Spratly Islands
featureList.countries: Disputed (China, Taiwan, Vietnam, Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei)
featureList.notes: Archipelago of >100 reefs, atolls, and islets in the South China Sea. Sits atop strategic maritime choke points and prospective oil/gas reserves. Flashpoint of Chinese artificial island building and runway construction.

featureList.name: Paracel Islands
featureList.countries: Disputed (Controlled by China; claimed by Vietnam & Taiwan)
featureList.notes: Archipelago of ~130 coral islands in the northern South China Sea. Controlled by China since the 1974 Battle of the Paracel Islands with South Vietnam. Heavily militarized with radar and surface-to-air missiles.

featureList.name: Great Victoria Desert
featureList.notes: Largest desert in Australia (~348,750 km²). Pristine arid wilderness characterized by sand dunes, gibber plains, and salt lakes. Site of British nuclear testing at Maralinga in the 1950s.

featureList.name: Great Dividing Range
featureList.notes: Australia's most substantial mountain chain, running >3,500 km parallel to the east coast. Forms the drainage divide between east-flowing coastal streams and the inland Murray-Darling River system. Mount Kosciuszko (2,228 m) is Australia's highest mainland peak.

featureList.name: Great Barrier Reef
featureList.notes: World's largest coral reef system (~2,300 km long, covering ~344,400 km² in the Coral Sea). Composed of >2,900 individual reefs and 900 islands. Highly vulnerable to climate change and marine heatwave coral bleaching events.

featureList.name: Murray River
featureList.notes: Australia's longest river (2,508 km). Rises in the Australian Alps, forms the border between New South Wales and Victoria, and empties into the Southern Ocean at Lake Alexandrina. Backbone of the Murray-Darling agricultural basin ('Food Bowl of Australia').

featureList.name: Darling River
featureList.notes: 3rd longest river in Australia (1,472 km). Major tributary of the Murray River, rising in southern Queensland. Subject to severe drought drying cycles and ecological fish die-off events.

featureList.name: Lake Eyre (Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre)
featureList.notes: Lowest natural point in Australia (-15 m below sea level) and largest lake in Australia when full (~9,500 km²). Huge endorheic salt basin in the arid Outback that fills completely only a few times each century during rare La Niña monsoonal flooding.

featureList.name: Tasmania
featureList.notes: Island state of Australia located 240 km south of the mainland, separated by Bass Strait. Known for pristine temperate wilderness (Tasmanian Wilderness UNESCO site) and hydro-industrial development.

featureList.name: New Zealand (North & South Islands)
featureList.notes: Comprises North Island (active volcanism, geothermal energy) and South Island (Southern Alps, Mount Cook/Aoraki), separated by Cook Strait. Part of the submerged continent of Zealandia.

featureList.name: Bass Strait
featureList.notes: Strait separating the state of Tasmania from the mainland of Australia (Victoria). Connects the Tasman Sea / Pacific with the Great Australian Bight / Southern Ocean. Major offshore oil and gas field (Bass Strait basin).

featureList.name: Torres Strait
featureList.notes: Narrow strait (~150 km wide) between the northern tip of Cape York Peninsula (Australia) and Papua New Guinea. Connects the Arafura Sea to the Coral Sea.

featureList.name: Cook Strait
featureList.notes: Strait separating the North and South Islands of New Zealand (~22 km wide at narrowest). Connects the Tasman Sea to the South Pacific Ocean. Notorious for unpredictable strong winds and tidal rip currents.
